title: [Retro P1] Treat findings inside the goal as ordinary rework; do not copy them into acceptance text
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

In B, when a finding went beyond the literal wording of the original acceptance, the Executor wrote that case into the acceptance text and then fixed the code. `US-S2-A2` grew from one sentence into an enumeration of malformed inputs close to 2000 characters. At 10:15 it hit the 2000-character limit, and the Executor shortened it by deleting words, such as changing "the Task" to "Task" (2107 → 2053 → 2006 → 1998).

Each such rewrite is a breaking Intent revision. B contains about 19 `approve_breaking_intent_revision` calls (including retries after hitting the limit), each one a native confirmation the user had to answer.

One of these revisions also turned a never-shipped "pre-marker mixed format" into an acceptance condition, and a finding in round 8 was raised on exactly that basis.

## Proposed handling

Distinguish two kinds of finding:

- A defect that falls inside the Intent's goal and `scope_hint` is ordinary rework. Fix the code, add tests, close the finding. The Intent is not revised.
- A breaking Intent revision is used only when the goal, the scope, or a user-visible commitment changes.

Acceptance text states principles. Enumeration of specific cases belongs in tests.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The contract (`imm-run` and the Executor/Reviewer role prompts) states this distinction, and states that a single input case must not be appended to acceptance in order to close a finding.
- [ ] Validate against the findings of rounds 9–12 in B: under the new rule none of them requires an Intent revision.
- [ ] A Reviewer can still raise a blocking finding for a defect that is inside the goal but not covered word for word by existing acceptance, and the Kernel does not reject it for lacking matching acceptance text.
- [ ] The 2000-character limit stays. Raising it is not the solution.

## Scope

P1; Owner: dereknex. Related: #189. Does not relax the breaking revision requirement when scope really grows.

title: [Retro P1] Batch authorization can delegate approval of in-Lane Intent revisions to the coordinator
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

Each of the roughly 19 `approve_breaking_intent_revision` calls in B required the user to go to the Lane tab and answer a native confirmation. A shows the Lane sitting in `blocked` waiting for that confirmation several times (10:07, 10:15, 10:20), with the coordinator able only to tell the user to go and answer it. The user's goal is batch implementation with as little human involvement as possible.

## Conflict with existing decisions

This issue changes accepted decisions and needs a new ADR first:

- ADR 0005 rejected a "batch-scoped authority record".
- ADR 0016 clause 6 states "No new authority tier".
- The acceptance of #178 states that breaking revisions go through the existing native gate and that production behavior is not relaxed to save confirmations.

## Proposed handling

In the single native confirmation that starts a batch, the user may also grant the coordinator one bounded permission: to approve a Lane's Intent revisions that stay inside the parent Spec and the child task's original `scope_hint`.

- The Kernel records the coordinator as the approver and references the batch authorization. It does not record the user.
- The coordinator does not send keys to a tab to answer a confirmation. Approval goes through a Kernel operation.
- Revisions outside the delegation (widening `scope_hint`, raising the risk level, changing a decision of the parent Spec) can still be approved only by the user.
- Host trust, login, and permission dialogs are outside the delegation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A new ADR explains why the relevant clauses of ADR 0005 and ADR 0016 are revised, and is accepted.
- [ ] The batch confirmation UI shows the delegation explicitly. The user can start a batch without granting it, and behavior is then identical to today.
- [ ] A delegated approval is distinguishable in the audit record from an approval by the user in person, and traces back to the specific batch authorization.
- [ ] Test for an out-of-bounds revision: delegated approval is refused and falls back to the user's native confirmation.
- [ ] The delegation expires when the batch terminates or is retired, and cannot be reused by a later batch.

## Scope

P1; Owner: dereknex. Related: ADR 0005, 0013, 0016, #178. The issue #193 removes most revisions first; this issue handles the rest.

title: [Retro P1] Coordinator can send text to a Lane session and is notified when a Lane becomes blocked
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

The Herdr Lane Tabs section of `imm-run.md` says the coordinator submits only the `imm-run` entry to a Lane and "sends that tab no keys and no prompt". The consequences:

- The user typed 6 messages in B in total. Three of them were corrections the coordinator wrote in A and the user pasted verbatim (07:44, 10:17, 10:29).
- Once a Lane stopped, the coordinator could only print text in A. The coordinator took no action between its conclusion at 07:16 and the user's next question at 07:39, nor between 07:40 and 10:05.
- At 10:05 the user asked the coordinator to monitor uas-s2 ("监控一下 uas-s2 的进度"), and only then did the coordinator discover the Lane was stopped on a confirmation.

## Proposed handling

1. Allow the coordinator to send a text instruction to a Lane session while it is idle. Native confirmations are not answered with keys (see the issue #194).
2. When a Lane becomes `blocked`, or becomes `idle` without having settled, the coordinator is woken and tells the user which tab, which `task_id`, and what it is waiting for.
3. Every instruction the coordinator sends is recorded in the batch report, so Executor-initiated behavior and coordinator intervention can be told apart afterwards.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The contract's Herdr Lane Tabs section is updated to state when text may be sent and which dialog types may not be answered.
- [ ] End-to-end verification that a Lane resumes after the coordinator sends a correction (parity between the two Hosts follows the existing parity convention).
- [ ] Test that the coordinator sends no input while a Lane is `blocked`.
- [ ] Both `blocked` and "idle without settle" wake the coordinator without depending on the user asking.
- [ ] Reviewer sessions still cannot be continued or re-prompted. That constraint is unaffected by this change.

## Scope

P1; Owner: dereknex. Related: ADR 0013, #170, #174.

title: [Retro P1] Coordinator takes over design judgment when the rework budget is exhausted, with a bounded number of attempts
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

In B, implementation took 10 minutes (05:33–05:43). The following 4 hours 50 minutes were spent in the Review loop: 12 Review rounds, Intent revised up to revision 15, 31 context compactions (about one per minute after 10:01). The Executor fixed findings one at a time and never made a design-level judgment.

The loop was broken twice, both times by an instruction the coordinator wrote in A and the user pasted into the Lane. At 07:44, "parse the visible Markdown" was replaced with a single marker source, and the parsing findings stopped. At 10:17, a hand-written second validator was replaced with reuse of `normalizeTaskScenarios`, and the loop converged within two rounds. By round 8 the coordinator could already show that 6 rounds of findings belonged to the same invariant.

`imm-run.md` already requires that on the second rework of the same acceptance id or anchor, the fix must state that it covers every trigger class of that invariant, or refute the finding with `refute_finding`. That rule did not stop the loop in B.

## Proposed handling

In batch Lane mode, when a child task exhausts its rework budget, it no longer stops and waits for the user. The coordinator takes over:

1. Read the findings from every round of the task and decide whether they point at one root cause.
2. Send the Lane one design-level correction (depends on the issue #195).
3. Start a new Lane session for each correction. State is read back from the Kernel and the staging area; the old context is not reused.
4. At most 2 corrections. If the task is rejected again after that, park the Slice, keep executing Slices that do not depend on it, and report everything at the end of the batch.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A Lane child task that exhausts its rework budget triggers a coordinator correction instead of `awaiting_user`. Single-task behavior outside a batch is unchanged.
- [ ] The correction count is recorded and enforced by the Kernel or the batch state, with a limit of 2. When the rework budget is exhausted a third time, the child task is parked with a park reason distinguishable from other reasons.
- [ ] Sibling Slices that do not depend on the parked child continue to execute and integrate.
- [ ] The Executor run after each correction is a new session, and a test proves it recovers from Kernel state and the Lane workspace alone.
- [ ] Establish why the existing "second rework must cover every trigger class" rule had no effect in B, and record the conclusion in this issue.

## Scope

P1; Owner: dereknex. Related: #187, #189. Depends on #195. Does not change Reviewer independence, and does not let the coordinator edit code on the Executor's behalf.

title: [Retro P1] In batch Lane mode, close a Child Issue only after its integration commit
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

In A, when S1 settled inside its Lane, the Executor closed #188 (around 03:52). The batch then judged S1 as `batch_lane_lost` because of the plugin cache mismatch, and the batch branch stayed at `eebc495` with no S1 commit. S1 was integrated as `475e346` only after re-authorization at 05:32.

For about 1 hour 40 minutes the tracker showed #188 as done while the code was not on the batch branch. Had the batch been abandoned at that point, the issue state would have been wrong.

## Proposed handling

In Lane mode, `mark-terminal` for a Child Issue is deferred until the batch has integrated that child's commit into the batch branch, and is performed on the coordinator side. Settling inside the Lane changes Kernel state only.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Settling inside a Lane produces no tracker write. After a successful integration the Child is closed exactly once.
- [ ] When a child task is judged `batch_lane_lost` or is parked, the Child stays open.
- [ ] Close timing for non-Lane batches and single tasks is unchanged.
- [ ] Parent closure is still done by the tracker's terminal-state projection, with unchanged rules.

## Scope

P1; Owner: dereknex. Related: #188, and Initiative Parent closure in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

title: [Retro P2] Reseal plan_digest at integration for in-Lane Intent revisions inside the delegation
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

In A, after S2 was integrated (`4d6fd0b`), provisioning the Lane for S3 was refused with `plan_digest mismatch` (10:39). The Intent that S2 revised inside its Lane entered the batch branch with the integration, while the batch authorization is bound to the revision and content hash of every child Intent.

Recovery followed ADR 0016: `retire_stale_batch` set the old batch to `superseded`, then a new batch was started. That cost two native confirmations and about 10 minutes, and left one retired batch behind. The same mismatch occurred in the #165 batch (see #178).

## Conflict with existing decisions

The Rejected Alternatives of ADR 0016 explicitly reject "auto-supersede at preflight" and "the runner retires on its own when it detects drift". The proposed handling in #178 says a `plan_digest` change continues to fail closed. This issue does not revive either rejected alternative, but it changes the premise that any revision invalidates the authorization. That has to be argued in the same ADR as #194.

## Proposed handling

An in-Lane revision approved under the batch delegation is itself a fact inside the scope of the batch authorization. When that child is integrated, the batch records its new revision and content hash in the batch record and reseals the digest. Later children continue normally.

Revisions not approved under the delegation (out-of-bounds revisions the user approved in person, or an Intent edited directly on the coordinator side) still fail closed as today and take the ADR 0016 retirement path.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Resealing happens only in the integration step and accepts only revisions that carry a delegated approval record. The batch record keeps the digest before and after each reseal.
- [ ] A regression test covers the scenario in A: S2 is revised in its Lane and integrated, then S3 is provisioned without retiring the old batch.
- [ ] An out-of-bounds revision still triggers `plan_changed`, and the retirement path is unchanged.
- [ ] Commit evidence and lineage of already integrated children are unchanged after a reseal.

## Scope

P2; Owner: dereknex. Depends on #194. Related: ADR 0005, 0016, #178, #181.

title: [Retro P2] Preflight the runtime contract version at batch start, and add a dedicated park reason for contract mismatch
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

In A, the Claude plugin driving the batch was the cached 5.1.0, while Pi in the Lane loaded the repository source. Both carried the same version number, but 22 runtime files differed: the Lane wrote `task_record/v4` and the cached plugin accepted only v3. Reading the Lane with the cached projection function gave `contract must equal assurance_kernel/task_record/v3; unknown field: git_base_head`.

The batch judged the Lane it could not read as `batch_lane_lost`. S1 was parked, and S2 and S3 were skipped. The batch made no progress from 03:52 to 05:32. Finding the root cause took the coordinator several rounds of investigation, because `batch_lane_lost` did not say the Lane was unreadable as opposed to missing.

## Proposed handling

1. Batch start preflight: before provisioning any Lane, compare the contract versions supported by the coordinator runtime and by the runtime the Lane Executor will load. On a mismatch, refuse and name the source path of each side.
2. Add a dedicated park reason for "Lane state exists but its contract version is not accepted by the coordinator", distinct from `batch_lane_lost`, carrying the original parse error.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fixture with a v3 coordinator and a v4 Lane reproduces the scenario in A: preflight refuses before any Lane is created.
- [ ] A case preflight does not cover (one side upgraded while the batch is running) is reported with the new park reason, not `batch_lane_lost`.
- [ ] When the contracts match, preflight adds no user confirmation.
- [ ] The comparison is based on the contract identifier, not the plugin version number (both sides had the same version number in A).

## Scope

P2; Owner: dereknex. Related: #181, ADR 0013. Does not address how the plugin cache itself gets updated.

title: Make Review authorization a literal-user foreground decision
body:
## Parent

#1

## What to build

Give a user awaiting Review authorization one foreground Tool interaction whose choices come from the literal user and whose pending operation is derived from the Assurance projection. The interaction must complete approve, rework, and reject outcomes while treating cancel as no decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Tool derives the unique pending Review authority operation from Kernel-owned facts and does not accept an Agent-supplied approval value.
- [ ] The card shows the Task, Review verdict, QA state, changed-scope summary, evidence references, and pending operation.
- [ ] Approve, rework, and reject produce distinct valid Kernel transitions.
- [ ] Cancel or UI abort leaves the Task awaiting user authority and performs zero protected writes.
- [ ] Foreground cancellation and the final non-cancellable authority commit boundary retain existing fail-closed semantics.
- [ ] The Footer remains empty and no detached work or polling is introduced.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

title: Wire task tier into Kernel review-gate (skip Review for Routine tasks)
body:
## Parent

Part of #16.

## What to build

Wire the task-tier classification function from #19 into the Kernel readiness gate. Today, the review obligation (`review_step`/`review_gate_pass`) is raised unconditionally for every task. After this ticket, it is only raised when the task's resolved tier is `material` or `critical`. When the resolved tier is `routine`, the review obligation is not raised — every other obligation (QA, Compounder) is unaffected. Tier is re-evaluated as changed paths accumulate over the task's lifetime, so a task that starts `routine` and later touches a listed path is upgraded and gets the review gate before completion. For tasks that do get the review obligation, the Review step's input scope is completely unchanged by this work.

This is the one ticket in this batch that actually changes routing behavior — keep it isolated from the classification logic (#19) so it can be reviewed and rolled back independently if needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Kernel readiness gate calls the tier classification function (#19) with the task's current changed paths and declared `risk`.
- [ ] The review obligation is raised when the resolved tier is `material` or `critical`, exactly as it is raised unconditionally today.
- [ ] The review obligation is not raised when the resolved tier is `routine`.
- [ ] QA and Compounder obligations are unaffected by tier in either case.
- [ ] A task that starts `routine` and later touches a listed Material/Critical path is upgraded to at least `material` and gets the review obligation before completion.
- [ ] The Review step's input scope (what context/bundle it receives when it does run) is unchanged from current behavior.
- [ ] `tests/kernel-readiness.test.ts` is extended with cases: routine-path-only task does not raise the obligation; a task touching a listed path raises it; an escalated `risk` field raises it without a listed path; declared `risk` cannot suppress the obligation once a listed path is touched; a task upgraded mid-lifecycle raises the obligation before completion.

## Blocked by

- #19 (task-tier classification function)

title: [Retro P2] In Lane mode, block edit/write outside the Lane root and auto-restore leaks with provable origin
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

In A, the Pi Executor for S1 began with 10 `edit` calls using absolute paths, writing early changes to 8 files into the coordinator checkout before moving its work into the Lane. The first batch re-entry was refused with `working tree has unstaged or untracked changes`.

The coordinator confirmed the origin from the Lane session record and file modification times, made a backup, and asked the user whether to restore. That question waited from 03:53 to 05:08. The refusal message suggests `git add`; following it would have carried an unreviewed old version into the batch branch.

S2 and S3 did not repeat this, but no constraint had been added to the entry prompt, so that was luck.

## Proposed handling

1. In the Pi extension and the corresponding Claude-side mechanism: in Lane mode, an `edit` / `write` whose resolved target path is outside the Lane root is refused, with the Lane path in the message. `bash` is not intercepted, and the contract says so plainly.
2. When the coordinator re-enters a batch and finds a dirty working tree: if every dirty file can be attributed to the write record of a Lane session of this batch, back the changes up as a patch, restore automatically, and record it in the batch report. Otherwise refuse as today and hand it to the user.
3. Change that refusal message so it no longer suggests `git add`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tests that an `edit` / `write` from inside a Lane to a coordinator checkout path is refused, one per Host.
- [ ] Auto-restore triggers only when the origin of every dirty file is provable. If any change of unknown origin is mixed in, no file is touched.
- [ ] The location of the backup patch is written to the batch report, and the restore is reversible.
- [ ] The user's own uncommitted changes in the coordinator workspace are never restored.

## Scope

P2; Owner: dereknex. Related: #188, ADR 0013. Does not build a general bash sandbox.

title: [Retro P3] Machine-checked scope disjointness, full verification after batch completion, and a host notice when a task is active
body:
## Problem and evidence

Source: Claude retro session `a62d90ca-5f15-4e17-87ed-40bb624eec41`, 2026-10-10. Original sessions: A `2bc3f86e-f041-4556-9beb-99d505db1097` (immune-brain coordinator, batch #187); B `01a1244d-173c-748a-a704-bc9325aa6ace` (Pi Executor of the S2 Lane); C `01a124ab-7692-7325-8ab0-1af16e5f677e` (Pi session in refine).

Three smaller gaps:

1. **Scope overlap is checked by hand.** During planning in A, the coordinator wrote in the review table that the source files, tests, and generated artifacts of S2 and S3 were disjoint and verified. In fact the `scope_hint` of both Intents contained `docs/specs/user-acceptance-scenarios.spec.md`. The batch therefore made S3 wait for S2, and `max_parallel=4` had no effect. #178 handled closure of `scope_hint` but did not cover overlap between sibling Slices.
2. **No full verification after batch completion.** At the end of A, `typecheck` and 5 related test files (162 tests) were run on the batch branch. The full `bun test` was not run. The test numbers for the final version of S2 came from the Executor's own report.
3. **Host notice when a task is active.** In C the user typed "继续" ("continue"). The new session did not read Kernel state first; it ran the tests and at 07:17:19 offered to commit. The QA and Review approvals for that task are recorded at 07:17:25 and 07:20:42, with completion at 07:20:43, none produced by C, which means another session was running assurance at the time. The user replied only at 07:22, so nothing went wrong. The contract says ordinary input does not implicitly resume a Managed task, and C did not violate that.

## Proposed handling

1. Before handoff, the Planner compares the `scope_hint` of every Intent in the same Initiative by machine and outputs the overlapping paths. Parallel grouping follows that result, and the review table no longer carries a hand-written "verified".
2. After all children of a batch are integrated, the coordinator runs the full `bun test` and `bun run typecheck` on the batch branch and writes the results into the batch completion report. On failure the batch is reported as not passed; integrated commits are not rolled back.
3. When the workspace has a non-terminal TaskRecord, the host reads the state before committing or modifying files inside that task's scope, and tells the user there is an active task and what its current obligation is.

## Acceptance

- [ ] With the S2 and S3 Intents from A as fixtures: the comparison reports the shared Spec path, and the Batch Plan orders them serially.
- [ ] The batch completion report contains the commands and results of the full test run and the type check. The test command comes from project convention and is not hard-coded.
- [ ] For item 3, first establish the identity and timeline of the other session in C, then decide whether the fix is contract wording or a Host hook. Record the result in this issue.
- [ ] Item 3 does not change the rule that ordinary input does not implicitly resume a Managed task.

## Scope

P3; Owner: dereknex. Related: #178, #166, #189. The three items are independent and can be implemented separately.

title: [Proposal] Jev-style decision models: unified application portfolio (advisory-only, outside Kernel authority)
body:
<!-- issue-triage:2026-11-03 -->
## Current state (2026-11-03)

This issue remains the single carrier for the decision-model programme (#204 plus the #286 expansion chapter below). The sections after this one are a historical proposal snapshot; where they disagree with this section, this section wins.

### Delivered

- #341 — shared decision-model component (`decide()`, Clef and fake providers, egress gate) and the A14 offline eval runner.
- #358 — decision-model Initiative #349, S1–S7: acceptance repeat series and the deterministic rework convergence trigger (S1, S2), the Jev provider (S3), the shared decision-eval harness (S4), and offline eval runners for A4, A16 and A15 (S5–S7).
- #368 — layered user and project configuration; decision-model profiles live in user config, the egress allowlist in project config.

No real-provider eval has run yet, and no corpus is committed. Every runner has been proved with the fake provider and a stubbed `fetch` only.

### Decisions (C1–C5)

- **C1 — adopted as planning scope only.** The fifteen points in §5 are the planning universe. Adoption authorises no implementation; each point still needs its own Spec/TaskIntent and an offline report before any live form.
- **C2 — already implemented in code.** `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/decision_model/contract.ts:10-12`: `pr_comment`, `issue_text`, `command_text` and `session_event` are non-sensitive and always allowed; `finding`, `diff`, `goal_scope` and `spec_source` leave the machine only when the project egress allowlist names them.
- **C3 — deferred.** A9 bidirectional tier advice and the 2026-10-12 revision remain a proposal.
- **C4 — deferred to Phase 2.** A5 sampling posture.
- **C5 — this body rewrite.** #204 stays the carrier; live slices become owned sub-issues one at a time, not all fifteen at once.

The earlier queue note (behind #260, #285, #244, #205) no longer applies: all four are closed. #284 continues to own the A1/A2/A3 Review verifier work and its eval.

### Live slice

- #379 — A15 first real-provider offline eval (`docs/plans/a15-real-eval.intent.json`, `docs/specs/a15-real-eval.spec.md`). It runs Clef over a corpus extracted from this repository's issues, compares with the `majority_class` baseline and commits the report. The repository's labels are heavily imbalanced (179 `ready_for_agent`, 2 `needs_spec`, 0 `duplicate` on 2026-11-03), so this run proves the real path end to end and records calibration data. It does not support a model-versus-baseline conclusion and sets no threshold.

### Deferred

- A9 (C3), A5 (C4).
- Human labelling and real runs for A14, A4 and A16.
- Per #349: A13, A8, A11, A10, A12, A6, A7, A1–A3 migration, A17, rework budget unit.

### Unchanged boundaries

- No live use of any point, including A14 in `fix-pr` and A4 as an Advisory.
- Model output never enters a TaskRecord, batch record or digest, and no authority path calls a model (ADR 0006).

---

## Summary

[Jev](https://beam.ai/agentic-insights/jev-typesafe-ai-agents) (TypeSafe AI) is a "decision model": it returns a probability per option from a closed option set instead of free text, and the caller's code owns the thresholds. This proposal records where such a model could help Immune-Brain's unattended path, and where it must not be used.

**Verdict.** It must not decide anything in the Kernel, the Batch Runner, or any authority gate. It may help in a few Host-native judgments that already belong to an LLM, under three conditions:

1. **Advisory only.** Its output never enters a TaskRecord, the batch record, or a digest.
2. **Escalation only.** It may make the flow stricter (raise risk, suggest stopping, ask for a design-level fix). It may never relax a check, skip a gate, or answer for the literal user.
3. **Measured offline first.** It is evaluated on recorded evidence before any Host integration.

The first item to do needs no model at all (S1 below).

## Why the core path is out of scope

- The core decisions are already deterministic and reproducible from recorded state:
  - `classifyIntentRevision` and `riskFloorForScope` (`runtime/kernel/intent.ts`)
  - Lane scope disjointness (`unattended/batch_schedule.ts`)
  - `plan_digest` and HEAD Lineage checks
  - the frozen reason table (`unattended/batch_reasons.ts`)
  - the Review rework park rule in `request_rework` (`runtime/kernel/reducer.ts`): `REVIEW_REWORK_ROUND_BUDGET = 5`, a repeated `security_boundary` parks the task, and live-refuted claims are not counted
- ADR 0006 §3: the runtime never invokes a model. ADR 0005 §6 and ADR 0016: user decisions, parked children, breaking revisions and batch retirement belong to the literal user. ADR 0017 binds the reviewer's own bytes.
- The real unattended failures in `docs/reports/pi-batch-execution-retro-2026-10-02.md` were deterministic defects, and the structured facts were already available. Examples: technical rework reported as a human decision while `open_user_decision_count=0`, and the authorization expiry bug. A probabilistic layer would not have fixed them.

## Evidence: multi-round Review rework

The question was whether the model should decide, round by round, whether rework continues. I read `.imm/audit/*/task-record.json` read-only, 145 records:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Tasks with at least one Review rework round | 59 (86 had none) |
| Tasks with 5 or more rounds | 12, of which 11 `done` and 1 `stopped` |
| Longest runs | 51, 22, 16, 14, 13 rounds |
| `authorize_rework` at the replan gate | 17, 13, 12, 10, … (users almost always chose to continue) |
| Refuted Review findings | 0 |

In the long tail, almost every round raised a new, real defect at a new anchor, but against one acceptance id:

- `2026-09-01-002-claude-code-host`: 64 blocking findings on `acc-claude-authority`
- `2026-09-08-002-initiative-amendment`: 45 on `acc-amendment-safety`
- `2026-09-05-003-batch-run-state-machine`: 19 on `acc-batch-run-stop-and-recovery`

This is whack-a-mole within one invariant class, not divergence. These tasks did complete. So a model that decides "stop" would mostly have cut off work that was going to finish, and in an unattended batch a park also turns every dependent into `skipped_blocked`. What wasted rounds was the late switch from point fixes to a fix of the shared guard. #196 records the same pattern: 12 rounds in Lane session B, and convergence only after a design-level correction.

Caveats: some records are v3 or predate the current 5-round budget, so their round counts do not compare directly with the current rule. Tokens and elapsed time were not measured.

## Proposed scenarios, in priority order

### S1 — Deterministic rework convergence signal (no model) · prerequisite

Add a read-only projection: for each `acceptance_id` (and anchor), the number of consecutive Review rounds that raised an effective blocking finding. Use it to trigger the existing `dist/imm-run.md` rule ("on the second rework of one acceptance id or anchor, the fix must cover every known trigger class of the invariant, or `refute_finding`"). Today that rule exists only as prompt text, and #196 asks why it had no effect.

- [ ] The Assurance or Inspect Projection exposes the per-acceptance repeat count. It is derived from TaskRecord findings and writes nothing.
- [ ] When the count reaches 2, the Parent/Executor handoff carries a design-level obligation: cover the invariant class or refute with evidence. The trigger is the count, not prompt memory.
- [ ] Replayed over the three long-tail records above, the signal fires by round 2–3.
- [ ] The rework budget, `replan_required`, and Review independence stay unchanged.

This gives #196 ("coordinator takes over design judgment") a deterministic trigger and evidence source.

### S2 — Offline evaluation of finding-equivalence classification (decision model, no runtime change)

The one judgment S1 cannot make deterministically: is a new blocking finding at a new anchor the same invariant class as an earlier one, a new defect, or outside the contract? The options form a closed set and the input is natural language, which suits a decision model.

- [ ] Hand-label the invariant classes of the findings in the 12 records with 5 or more rounds, plus Lane session B from #196.
- [ ] Measure whether a Jev-style classifier (and, as a baseline, the Reviewer's own declared invariant class) groups them correctly by round 2–3.
- [ ] Estimate the rounds saved if a design-level correction had been issued at the first correct grouping.
- [ ] Record the result in this issue. No Host or runtime code changes in S2.

### S3 — Parent-side advisory integration (only if S2 shows a clear gain)

After a rework verdict is submitted and before the Executor edits, the Parent (or the #196 coordinator) receives the classification as advisory input. It chooses between a point fix and a shared-guard fix, and decides what goes into the single design-level correction #196 allows.

- [ ] The output is recorded only as advisory evidence: never a Finding disposition, never `replan_required`, never a TaskRecord field.
- [ ] It cannot suppress, downgrade or dedupe Reviewer findings (ADR 0017), cannot answer `authorize_rework` or any native gate, and cannot extend the rework budget.
- [ ] If the classifier is unavailable or fails, behavior is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] A suggestion to escalate early needs a high threshold, and becomes "change fix strategy" before "park".

### S4 — `imm-pr-fix` PR comment triage (independent, low risk)

Classify each PR comment as blocking, nit, out of scope, or a duplicate before deciding what to fix. `imm-pr-fix` is a standalone Host-native Skill outside Managed authority, and misclassification is cheap and visible. This is the easiest place for a live pilot.

- [ ] Evaluate offline against historical PR comments first.
- [ ] Never resolve a red-circle or security finding on the classifier's word alone.

### S5 — Escalation-only advisories (optional, lower priority)

- **Planner risk:** suggest raising `routine` to `material`, never lowering. Same direction as `riskFloorForScope`. The Planner still owns the risk tier.
- **Lane command risk:** the Executor Host may stop a Lane and report when a command scores high-risk. It must never auto-approve anything beyond the user's own settings. This matches the ADR 0013 revision: dialogs are reported, never answered.

## Explicitly rejected uses

- Replacing the Kernel continue/park decision in `request_rework`, or changing the budget at runtime from a model score.
- Pre-filtering Reviewer findings ("this rework isn't worth it"), or rewriting or deduplicating verdict bytes.
- Answering `replan_required`, `authorize_rework`, breaking Intent revision, or any literal-user gate, even though history shows users mostly chose "continue". That history is input for tuning the deterministic rule, not for automating the gate.
- Any model call from `runtime/`, `runtime/kernel/`, or `runtime/unattended/`.

## Open questions

- Is the historical "users almost always continue" signal better addressed by changing `REVIEW_REWORK_ROUND_BUDGET`, or by counting per acceptance id instead of per round? That would be a deterministic rule change and would need its own decision.
- Hosted model dependency: network, cost, and what diff or finding text is sent off-machine. These must be settled before S3 or S4 go live.

## Related

#196 (coordinator design judgment on budget exhaustion), #193 (in-goal findings as ordinary rework), #51 (Review convergence, closed via #62), ADR 0005 / 0006 / 0013 / 0016 / 0017.

## Status

Proposal for discussion. No Spec, TaskIntent, Enrollment, or implementation is authorized by this issue. Jev's capabilities and benchmark numbers are taken from third-party write-ups and are not verified.

---

## Expansion chapter imported from #286 (historical proposal snapshot)

下文完整保留 #286 的应用组合、设计、风险和 C1–C5，以免归并丢失内容。历史段落中的“until C5 is decided / #204 stands unchanged”已被本票顶部的载体归并决定替代；其余待决策项仍待决定，不因保留文本而获批准。历史 phase 的 r2 待办描述已过时，当前实现顺序以上方 triage 为准。

## Provenance

- 2026-10-20, Derek directed: submit this complete application proposal as an issue.
- Status: proposal for discussion and decision. No Spec, TaskIntent, Enrollment, or implementation is authorised by this issue; §10 lists the decisions (C1–C5) that would activate it.
- Origin: issue #204 is the pattern source and remains an open proposal; three instances of the pattern are already adopted and designed in #284. This proposal consolidates the 2026-10-20 decision-model survey of this repository (all 213 issues, 27 ADRs, the full spec/contract/code decision surface) with the Jev expansion map and capability analysis produced the same day.
- Relation to #204: §10 C5 proposes this plan become #204's expansion chapter under the disposition set out in the decision-models unified plan; until Derek decides C5, #204 stands unchanged.

---

decision-models unified plan and the Jev expansion/design plan of the
same date. It authorises nothing by itself; §10 lists the decisions
that would activate it. Pattern source: issue #204. Working precedent:
the three instances adopted in #284.

## 1. Summary and verdict

Immune-Brain's authority decisions are deterministic by design and
must stay that way. But a residue of real judgments in the system is
made today by LLMs or by humans scanning lists — unmeasured,
uncalibrated, and expressed as free text or gut feel. [Jev]
(https://beam.ai/agentic-insights/jev-typesafe-ai-agents)-style
decision models address exactly that residue: given a closed option
set, the model returns a probability per option; the caller's code
owns the thresholds; every use is evaluated offline against recorded
evidence before it is allowed to influence anything.

**Verdict.** Adopt Jev-style models as the project's single approved
pattern for probabilistic assistance, in the fifteen application
points mapped in §5, under the constitution in §3, delivered in the
phases in §7. The pattern never enters the Kernel, the Batch Runner,
or any authority gate (ADR 0006 stands untouched). Three instances
are already adopted and designed (#284); this proposal completes
#204's original programme and adds six new application points where
the same admission criteria pass.

## 2. Evidence: why this pattern, why now

1. **The whack-a-mole data (#204, re-read from 145 audit records).**
   59 tasks had at least one Review rework round; the long tail (51,
   22, 16 rounds) was almost entirely *repeated new defects in one
   invariant class against one acceptance* — 64 blocking findings on
   a single acceptance in the worst record. The deterministic half of
   the fix (per-acceptance repeat counts) is now #284 S1 item 7; the
   semantic half (is this new finding the same class?) is a judgment
   no deterministic rule can make and an LLM today makes implicitly,
   in prose, inside the rework loop — precisely a Jev-shaped hole.
2. **#196's correction had no trigger.** The coordinator's
   design-level takeover converged the 12-round Lane session, but
   fired on a human noticing a pattern. Repeat counts (data) plus
   equivalence classification (probability) are the trigger and the
   aim.
3. **Passes are never verified.** #284's verifier, by decision D6,
   examines only `rework` verdicts. A `pass` is the one consequential
   judgment in the review pipeline with no second look and no
   measurement — an audit-sampling-shaped hole (A5 in §5).
4. **Decisions are unmeasured where they are probabilistic.** The
   2026-10-20 measurement over the committed audit records could not
   recover even the *duration* of a review from the records, and
   #177 item 4 / #164 (designed measurement windows) never ran. The
   project's deterministic decisions are auditable to the byte; its
   probabilistic ones are auditable not at all. This proposal's eval
   infrastructure (§6) is the same investment as fixing that.
5. **The pattern has already survived contact.** In #284, three
   Jev-style items were designed into a critical-path initiative
   without bending any authority rule: a pre-screen whose output is
   forbidden from becoming a label, a mislabel metric fenced as
   experimental until scored, and one escalation check whose only
   power is to convert an archive into an existing user dispute. The
   constitution held; the proposal generalises from a working sample,
   not from the vendor's write-up (whose benchmark claims #204
   already flags as unverified).

## 3. The constitution (does not change under this proposal)

From #204, verbatim in effect:

1. **Advisory only.** Model output never enters a TaskRecord, a batch
   record, or a digest. (Recorded refinement, from #284 S3: a score
   may be written into a history event as a pure observation, beside
   its threshold version.)
2. **Escalation only.** A score may make a flow stricter — add a
   check, stop and report, route to the literal user. It may never
   relax a check, skip a gate, suppress or downgrade a finding, or
   answer for the user.
3. **Measured offline first.** No live influence before an offline
   evaluation on recorded evidence, against a named baseline.

Plus the one fenced exception already argued in #204's own revision
thread: *bidirectional advice on the Planner's risk tier* (A9 in §5).
The tier is today a model's free declaration; advising that same
judgment in both directions does not touch authority, because the
Kernel floor applies after the advice regardless. The exception is
limited to that surface and is decided separately (§10, C3).

**Admission criteria** — an application point is in scope only if all
hold: (A1) the judgment already belongs to a model or a human today;
(A2) the option set is closed and small; (A3) error costs are
asymmetric and threshold-expressible; (A4) labels exist or can be
built from records; (A5) classifier absence degrades to
byte-identical baseline behaviour; (A6) an existing decider or stop
receives the output; (A7) data egress for the input class is settled
(§10, C2).

## 4. What the model class can do (capability spectrum)

Judging is one capability of six families this plan draws on:

- **Discrimination** — classification; equivalence/grouping;
  consistency checking; anomaly detection ("none of the above" when
  every option scores low).
- **Ordering & allocation** — prioritisation; spending scarce budget
  (review rounds, attention, labelling hours) proportional to
  probability × cost; sampling design / active learning (choosing
  what to measure next).
- **Prediction & counterfactuals** — outcome forecasting for
  planning; trajectory signals across repeated scorings; offline
  policy evaluation (replay history under a candidate threshold
  before adopting it).
- **Control** — threshold triggering and routing; escalation;
  graduated autonomy (confidence decides *who* decides — used here
  only upward); abstention ("uncertain" as a designed, routable
  output).
- **Measurement** — offline rates no one could count by hand; drift
  monitoring of score distributions; calibration auditing
  (probabilities can be checked against outcomes; prose cannot).
- **Governance** — auditable replay via the score envelope (§6);
  policy-as-code (a threshold change is a reviewable, testable,
  revertible diff); composability (scores are numbers: they combine
  with deterministic counts and cost matrices without contract
  changes).

Hard limits of the class, accepted by this plan: it does not
generate (no rationales or fixes; probabilities are the whole
explanation surface), it does not act (all effects occur in caller
code), and it does not learn online (improvement flows only through
the offline eval loop).

## 5. Application portfolio (fifteen points)

Forms: **OFF** = offline-eval tooling · **HOST** = Host-side check
that can convert a next step into an existing stop · **ADV** =
advisory input to an existing decider. Status: **ADOPTED** = designed
in #284 · **#204** = proposed there · **NEW** = added by this plan.

### Review plane
| ID | Application | Form | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Gold-case selection pre-screen, uncertainty-first | OFF | ADOPTED (#284 S0⑦) |
| A2 | `security_boundary` mislabel rate | OFF | ADOPTED (#284 S1⑥) |
| A3 | Refutation escalation check → literal-user dispute | HOST | ADOPTED (#284 S3⑦) |
| A4 | Finding invariant-class equivalence → generalize-or-refute trigger + coordinator correction aim | OFF→ADV | #204 S2/S3 |
| A5 | Clean-pass audit sampling: missed-defect probability on `pass` → one added independent review over threshold, plus a small random sample for calibration | HOST | NEW |
| A6 | Review-depth routing advice: security-surface probability → advise stronger/security-emphasis review dispatch (makes #284 D1 per-dispatch) | ADV | NEW |

### Planning plane
| ID | Application | Form | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A7 | Intent-bounce prediction: breaking-revision / `replan_required` probability → advise clarify-or-split before Enrollment | ADV | NEW |
| A8 | Child-size scoring at batch planning: budget-overrun / park probability → advise split or reorder | ADV | NEW |
| A9 | Planner risk-tier advice, bidirectional, own offline eval; Planner decides, floor applies after | OFF→ADV | #204 S5 as revised 2026-10-12 |

### Execution plane
| ID | Application | Form | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A10 | Lane command risk → stop Lane and report; never auto-approves beyond user settings (ADR 0013) | HOST | #204 S5 |
| A11 | Park/conflict prediction per child → Parent's serial/Lane, ordering, and serialisation advice (deterministic scope overlap stays code) | ADV | NEW |
| A12 | QA failure classification {real, environment, flake}: may suggest one extra rerun or escalation; may never mark a failure passed | ADV | NEW |
| A13 | Scope-drift scoring for #278's beyond-estimate disclosure | OFF→HOST | NEW (after #278) |

### Repository operations (outside Managed authority)
| ID | Application | Form | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A14 | `imm-pr-fix` PR comment triage {blocking, nit, out-of-scope, duplicate}; never resolves a security/red-circle finding on the score alone | ADV | #204 S4 |
| A15 | Issue-triage classification {duplicate-of, severity suggestion, missing-information} for a human triager; and rework root-cause classification {spec ambiguity, implementation, environment} as a retro metric | OFF/ADV | NEW |

Every point names, before any live form: its label source (audit
records for A1–A9/A12/A13/A15; batch records for A8/A11; PR history
for A14; tracker history for A15), its baseline (including, where one
exists, the incumbent model's own declared label — #204 S2's
baseline), and its quality gate (§6).

## 6. Reference architecture

- **Three deployment forms only** (§5). A runtime form is forbidden
  (ADR 0006); there is no fourth.
- **Score envelope.** Any score that influences anything carries
  `{option set, probabilities, model id + version, threshold-set
  version}`, written to the form's log surface (eval report, advisory
  log, or a history event as observation). Envelopeless scores are
  not actionable.
- **Threshold registry.** Thresholds are code-owned, versioned
  constant sets — one home per application, registered in the
  decision registry (unified plan S0). A threshold changes only via
  a committed eval report showing the application's own quality
  metric does not worsen. Threshold *values* are set from baseline
  data at implementation time, never fixed in this proposal (A3's
  unset threshold is the correct posture).
- **Shared eval infrastructure.** #284 S0/S1 (corpus, gold labels,
  runner, baseline report) is the template for all review-plane
  points and the methodological template for the rest. No application
  builds a private measurement path.
- **Lifecycle and retirement.** offline eval → shadow (logged,
  shown to no decider) → advisory live → periodic re-evaluation.
  Retirement is designed in: acceptance rate near zero, precision
  below its gate, or label drift turns the application off; absence
  restores baseline by construction.

## 7. Phasing and gates

- **Phase 0 (in flight).** #284's A1/A2/A3; #204 S1's deterministic
  trigger wiring (the rail A4 rides). Gate to Phase 1: #284 S1
  baseline committed.
- **Phase 1 (complete #204's programme).** A4 (offline first; ADV
  only on a measured gain), A14 (the low-risk live pilot), A9
  (offline eval first). Gate: each point's offline report shows the
  pre-registered gain or the point stops at offline.
- **Phase 2 (strongest new fits).** A5 (closes the review design's
  one unverified direction) and A11 (lands on the Parent's most
  frequent discretionary decision). Gate: Phase 1 framework habits
  proven; A5's sampling budget set from the #284 S1 baseline.
- **Phase 3 (breadth, on evidence).** A6, A7, A8, A12, A15; A13 joins
  whenever #278 lands.

No phase displaces the recorded execution priorities (#260 item 1,
then r2's remaining children). Jev applications are advisory
infrastructure and queue behind correctness work.

## 8. Risks and mitigations

- **Egress / hosted dependency** (#204's open question): live forms
  send finding, diff, or command text off-machine. Mitigation:
  per-input-class decision (§10 C2) before any live form; offline
  forms never wait on it; command text and PR comments are the
  low-sensitivity classes, diff/finding text defaults to the
  reviewer's own trust domain.
- **Miscalibration**: an overconfident score is worse than none.
  Mitigation: calibration auditing is part of every eval (§4,
  Measurement); a point whose calibration fails its gate stays
  offline.
- **Escalation fatigue**: advisory stops that users always dismiss
  train dismissal. Mitigation: acceptance rate is a first-class
  metric with a retirement trigger (§6); thresholds are set from
  data to keep escalation volume honest.
- **Scope creep toward gates**: each success invites "let it decide".
  Mitigation: the constitution (§3) plus admission criteria (§3) are
  the review checklist for any new point; the decision registry
  records every point's plane, and P5's definition excludes
  authority by construction.
- **Threshold gaming / drift**: labels age as the codebase and
  reviewers change. Mitigation: periodic re-evaluation in the
  lifecycle; drift monitoring on score distributions; retirement.

## 9. Explicitly rejected

Incorporating #204's rejected list, plus this plan's additions:
replacing or retuning at runtime any Kernel continue/park decision
or budget; pre-filtering, rewriting, or deduplicating Reviewer
verdict bytes; answering any literal-user gate; any model call from
`runtime/`; a symmetric QA classifier that could waive a failure
(A12 is one-directional by design); merge-conflict *resolution*
(prediction A11 is advice; resolution belongs to #275/#277);
scoring the delivered predicate or prerequisite checks (#254/#285);
and any use on low-frequency one-off decisions, where admission
criterion A4 fails by construction.

## 10. Decisions requested

- **C1 — Adopt the portfolio.** §5's fifteen points as the planning
  universe, phased per §7. (Recommendation: adopt.)
- **C2 — Egress policy by input class.** Command text and PR
  comments may use a hosted scorer; diff/finding text stays within
  the reviewer's trust domain unless separately approved. No live
  form ships for a class before its decision. (Recommendation:
  adopt as stated.)
- **C3 — Bidirectional tier advice (A9).** Fold Derek's 2026-10-12
  revision into #204's body and Phase 1. (Recommendation: adopt;
  same question as the unified plan's D5.)
- **C4 — A5 sampling posture.** Threshold-triggered sampling plus a
  small random calibration sample, the rate itself set from the S1
  baseline at Phase 2 design time. (Recommendation: adopt the
  posture; fix no number now.)
- **C5 — Carrier and #204 disposition.** This proposal becomes the
  expansion chapter folded into #204 (which then executes the
  unified plan's S1 disposition: body rewritten to current state,
  live slices as owned children), and the P5 section of the decision
  registry (unified plan S0) cites it as source. (Recommendation:
  adopt.)

## Appendix: cross-references

- Pattern and evidence: #204 (incl. 2026-10-12 revision comment and
  2026-10-20 S1-split pointer comment).
- Adopted instances and eval infrastructure: #284 (S0⑦, S1⑥⑦⑧,
  S3⑦; decisions D1–D6).
- Deterministic partners: #196 (coordinator correction), #284 S1
  item 7 (repeat-count data), #204 S1 (trigger wiring).
- Sequencing neighbours: #260 item 1 and #273 (r2) ahead in the
  execution queue; #278 gates A13; #275/#277 own conflict mechanics.
- Taxonomy home: decision-models unified plan (five planes; Jev is
  P5), S0 registry and S6 standing rules.

title: Vibe coding 测试膨胀治理：分层落位与新增 imm-test-prune 技能
body:
<!-- issue-triage:2026-10-27 -->
## Current triage / remaining scope

**队列 5：#260 items 2–5 完成后、#284 主线之前收口。** 当前 main `d62c092` 已有 `imm-test-prune`、registry 派生技能列表、Executor / Review 测试约束及 `scripts/test-size-report.ts`。下方历史未勾选清单不代表这些交付仍全部缺失。

剩余明确缺口：只读报告尚无“单 PR 新增测试行数 / 改动行数比例”。补齐该项，复核已有接入清单与相关 focused checks 后关闭；不重建技能，不发起全仓测试批量清理。mutation testing、运行时间预算维持原票可选项，不新增关闭门槛。本次仅收敛待办，不启动实现。

---

## 背景

vibe coding 过程中，测试几乎可以零成本生成，删除测试却没有明确的负责人。agent 每次改动都会顺手加用例，很少合并或退休旧测试，测试规模因此单向增长。

### 本仓库现状（2026-10-10 统计）

- `tests/` 下有 166 个测试文件，约 1871 个 `it/test`，总计约 6.2 万行。非测试 TS 代码约 4.1 万行。
- 最大的测试文件：`tests/unattended-batch-commit.test.ts`（3521 行）、`tests/dual-host-assurance-conformance.test.ts`（2952 行）、`tests/plugin-package-runtime.test.ts`（2487 行）、`tests/unattended-batch-run.test.ts`（2378 行）。
- 共 38 个 `*-contract.test.ts`，另有 91 个测试文件直接读取 `.md`。`toContain(` 约 2000 处，`not.toContain(` 约 380 处，说明大量测试在锁定文档措辞。
- 每新增一个公共技能，都要手改约 5 个测试文件里写死的技能名数组，包括 `skill-dist-consistency`、`claude-host-package`、`pi-canary-packed-loader`、`direct-first-routing-contract`、`role-prompt-bridge`。

## 改进方法

1. **生成阶段**：每个测试只对应一条可观察行为或一个 bug；不镜像实现细节；新增测试前先查已有覆盖，优先扩展现有用例或参数化。
2. **结构层**：同构用例改为 `test.each` 表驱动；重复 setup 收敛到 `tests/helpers` 下的 builder；文档契约测试从逐句 `toContain` 改成结构校验（frontmatter、链接、必需章节、镜像一致性）；快照只用于稳定的机器输出。
3. **维护层**：测试跟随行为一起退休（AGENTS.md 已有此规则）；临时测试写明退出条件；用 per-test 覆盖数据找出被其他测试完全包含的用例，作为合并候选，人工确认后再处理。
4. **度量层**：报告测试/源码行数比、单文件行数上限、单 PR 新增测试行数与改动行数的比例。可以用 mutation testing 衡量新增测试是否真的提高了保护力，也可以设测试运行时间预算。
5. **工作流层**：写测试和评审测试由不同角色负责；用小步 TDD，不在实现完成后再“补全测试”。

## 方案：分层沉淀，不全部塞进一个技能

AGENTS.md 规定技能只在显式触发时加载，所以“生成时少写测试”这类约束不能只放在技能里。

| 方法 | 落位 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| 单行为、不镜像实现、先查已有覆盖 | AGENTS.md 与 `plugins/immune-brain/dist/role-prompts` 的 Executor 提示词 | 每次写代码都要生效 |
| 新增测试是否重复、是否锁定实现细节 | Review 角色检查清单 | 写和评分离，复用 Finding 机制 |
| 行为退休时同步删测试 | AGENTS.md（已有） | 无需重复 |
| **存量审计、合并、删除** | **新技能 `imm-test-prune`** | 低频、需批准、有破坏性，与 `imm-doc-prune` 同形态 |
| 测试规模度量 | `scripts/` 下的只读报告脚本 | 机械统计，不需要 LLM，也不进入技能 |
| 可复用规律 | Compounder 写入 `docs/solutions/` | 复用现有 Learning 机制 |

## `imm-test-prune` 技能草案（沿用 `imm-doc-prune` 骨架）

**结构**（依据 ADR-0002）：`skills/imm-test-prune/SKILL.md` 是约 25 行的路由入口；`plugins/immune-brain/dist/imm-test-prune.md` 是完整契约。

**契约章节**：
- **Authority Boundary**：不创建或修改 TaskIntent、TaskRecord、Kernel。与当前 Managed 任务 `scope_hint` 重叠的候选标为 `BLOCKED_ACTIVE_SCOPE`。
- **Invocation**：只能显式调用。`imm-test-prune audit` 只读，产出 manifest 后停止；`imm-test-prune` 需要用户逐条批准 manifest。
- **Inventory and Manifest**：
  - 将测试分为四类：行为测试、文档契约测试、打包/镜像一致性测试、历史证据测试（如 frozen reader）。
  - 机械缩小候选：同构用例、重复 setup、逐句文档断言、可从 `registry.yaml` 派生的硬编码列表、失去保护对象的孤立测试。
  - **证据规则**：年龄、行数、偶发失败都不能单独作为删除依据。删除必须说明“行为已退休”或“由某测试继续覆盖”，最好附覆盖数据或 mutation 证据。
  - manifest 分类：`MERGE` / `PARAMETERIZE` / `EXTRACT_HELPER` / `RELAX_TO_STRUCTURE` / `DELETE` / `KEEP` / `BLOCKED` / `UNVERIFIED`。
- **Mutation Envelope**：只改测试、fixture 和 helper；需要改运行时、公共 API 或 Kernel 时停止。**不得为了通过而弱化断言。**
- **Verify and Report**：受影响的测试和相关回归全部通过，并跑 `bun run typecheck` 与 `git diff --check`。报告前后用例数、行数和耗时，以及每条删除的去向。不提交。
- **与 `imm-doc-prune` 的分工**：纯文档措辞测试归 doc-prune（其 Mutation Envelope 已经覆盖），测试结构和行为覆盖归 test-prune，两者在契约中互相写明边界。

## 接入清单

参照 `.imm/audit/2026-08-26-001-add-imm-doc-prune` 的改动面：

- [ ] `skills/registry.yaml` 新增条目（`role: execute`、`role_class: repair`、`output_artifacts: [test_prune_report]`、`next_actions: []`）
- [ ] `skills/imm-test-prune/SKILL.md` 与 `plugins/immune-brain/skills/imm-test-prune/SKILL.md`
- [ ] `plugins/immune-brain/dist/imm-test-prune.md`，在 `scripts/dist-sync-manifest.ts` 中登记，并通过 `scripts/sync-dist-docs.ts --check`
- [ ] 更新 `CONTEXT.md` 的 Architecture Map Public entries、`README.md`、`README.zh-CN.md`、`docs/reference/immune-brain-skills-guide.md`、`plugins/immune-brain/USER_GUIDE.md`、`plugins/immune-brain/dist/imm-run.md` 中 standalone 技能列表
- [ ] 新增 `tests/imm-test-prune-contract.test.ts`，更新上述测试里的技能列表
- [ ] 在 AGENTS.md、Executor 提示词和 Review 检查清单中加入生成阶段约束
- [ ] `scripts/` 下新增测试规模报告脚本（只读，不阻断）

## 建议的首个落地切片

先把 5 个测试文件里写死的技能名数组改为从 `registry.yaml` 派生。这一步既能验证本方法，也能降低之后接入 `imm-test-prune` 的成本。

## 推进方式

改动涉及公共技能面和打包契约，建议走 Managed Path：用 `imm-planner` 写 TaskIntent，每条 Acceptance Descriptor 绑定 focused test，再交给 `imm-run` 执行。

## Out of scope

- 不引入 CI 阻断门禁，度量脚本先只做报告。
- 不对全仓测试做一次性批量删除。

title: [phase-entry] Human-launched planning and execution
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=explicit-phase-entry -->

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

Recent Claude Code and Pi sessions went from a design confirmation straight to Enrollment and implementation without the user entering imm-run. The Planner contract tells the model to invoke Enrollment for execution-bearing requests, the explicit-entry rule is prose only, and neither Host checks that the user launched the run phase.

## Result

A design confirmation ends with candidate artifacts. Implementation starts only when the user enters imm-run and confirms the native Enrollment dialog. Both Hosts refuse Enrollment and batch start before any dialog when the session has no live run entry, and Claude Code denies a model-initiated Skill entry.

## Initiative design

Spec: docs/specs/explicit-phase-entry.spec.md. Invariants: no Enrollment or batch-start dialog opens without a live run entry; only literal user input creates or revokes an entry; a missing store, hook observation or admission is a refusal; the gate adds no authority; batch-internal enrollment is not gated. Slices run serially: S1 changes the contract text, S2 adds the shared phase-entry module and the Claude Code gate, S3 adds the Pi gate. S2 depends on S1 so the contract never instructs a call the gate refuses; S3 reuses the S2 module.

## Decisions

- Enrollment moves from the Planner to the first step of imm-run.
- A run entry is a session-scoped credential; a later Planner or Brainstorm entry in the same session revokes it. Each Slice still passes its own native Enrollment dialog.
- Model self-entry is blocked on Claude Code by a PreToolUse gate on the Skill tool rather than a frontmatter flag, so user aliases keep working.
- The gate sits at the Host tool boundary, not inside Kernel enrollment.

## Testing strategy

Contract tests over every packaged copy for S1; unit tests on the pure entry module plus hook-output and tool-handler tests that assert the dialog port is never reached for S2 and S3; one cross-Host equality check on the refusal code and recovery action; one manual scenario in real sessions.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-1` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: the user replies with a confirmation without entering imm-run. Then: no Enrollment dialog opens and the reply names imm-run as the next user action.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: the user enters imm-run or an alias for it. Then: the native Enrollment dialog opens and implementation proceeds once confirmed.
- `SCN-3` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: the user asks to continue with the next Slice. Then: that Slice's Enrollment dialog opens without a new imm-run entry.
- `SCN-4` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: the model calls the Skill tool for the Planner. Then: the call is denied with phase_entry_required.
- `SCN-5` (Slice `S3`, manual): When: the user replies with a confirmation. Then: the turn ends with candidate artifacts and no Enrollment dialog.

## Out of scope

- Kernel enrollment validation, QA, Review and completion authority.
- Blocking the Pi model from reading packaged Skill files.
- Untracked local alias files.

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: Every packaged contract copy makes the Planner stop after validation and makes Enrollment the first step of imm-run.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: On Claude Code, Enrollment and batch start are refused before any dialog without a live run entry, and model Skill self-entry is denied. (blocked by: explicit-phase-entry-s1-contract)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S3 --> **S3**: On Pi, Enrollment and batch start are refused before the authority dialog without a live run entry, with the same refusal as Claude Code. (blocked by: explicit-phase-entry-s2-claude-gate)

---

_Outbound visibility only: GitHub state never authorizes or settles work — Kernel TaskIntent, TaskRecord, QA, Review, and Assurance remain the execution authority. An Open Issue only means the Task still needs attention; only a claimless terminal projection closes it (`done` → Completed, `stopped` → Not planned)._

title: Add read-only imm-kernel inspect for current Kernel facts
body:
## Problem

Authors auditing Kernel safety machinery cannot see current claim, Assurance, or risk-floor facts without reading store files. `imm-kernel status --json` only reports layout, claim, and workspace. Task Rail is State / Result / Next. This is independent of #16 (Kernel dedup + task-tier); #16 is the visualization subject, not the parent spec.

## Result

`imm-kernel inspect --json` returns `assurance_kernel/inspect/v1`: layout, claim, workspace, Assurance Projection when a task is claimed, today's risk vs RISK_FLOOR_SCOPE_PREFIXES, and unobservable markers for Capability, rehearsal, and CAS holder state.

## Decisions

- Machine JSON only; `status --json` unchanged
- Current workspace claim only; idle still emits floor prefixes and does not fabricate a task
- Unreadable claimed record or intent fails closed; zero writes
- Compose existing read APIs in the Kernel CLI command surface; no new Kernel authority module
- Do not implement #16, restore progress UI, serialize Capability, or change CAS

## Testing

Focused `bun test tests/kernel-inspect.test.ts`: contract, idle floor prefixes, claimed risk resolution, fail-closed unreadable state, zero writes, missing `--json` rejected, `status --json` unchanged.

## Out of scope

TUI overlay, pretty-print, `--task-id`, Capability debug hook, CAS changes, #16 dedup/tier wiring, GitHub tracker visualization, TaskRecord dumps, legacy progress/Footer/polling.

## Authority boundary

Inspect is a read projection, not workflow authority. Enrollment, QA, Review, and settlement stay on TaskIntent / TaskRecord / Assurance Projection.

title: [ceremony-trim] Reduce ineffective ceremony found in the r647 retro
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=ceremony-trim-r647 -->

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

A retro of one planning session and one execution session on a consumer repository found four costs with no matching protection. A QA prepare timeout returned only byte counts, so the Executor guessed at the cause and retried blindly. Adding three re-export files to an enrolled scope took a breaking revision that was refused before its confirmation opened; across this repository 25 of 67 TaskIntents were revised at least once. A Planner session edited the files of a task another session was executing, and an instruction given there never reached the Executor. The contracts require text (Delivery Evidence before the first Assurance attempt, a reason for not drawing a diagram) that nothing reads.

## Result

A failed QA prepare stage can be located from its result; a sibling-file scope addition needs no confirmation while every wider change still does; a Planner session cannot edit an executing task's files; the Loop and Planner contracts drop three unused requirements.

## Initiative design

Spec: docs/specs/ceremony-trim-r647.spec.md. Invariants: no verifier output reaches TaskRecord, findings, audit evidence, batch state or tracker projection; the check stage returns no output text; a scope revision that removes an entry, adds a glob, enters a new directory or touches a risk-floor path stays breaking; every self-served scope addition is named in the next Review prompt. Slices run serially S1, S2, S3, S4 because all four edit the Loop or Planner contract; the machine overlap check reports six overlapping pairs and four single-task groups. S2 is the only Slice that changes an authority rule and records it in ADR 0021.

## Decisions

- The prepare stage may return a bounded stderr tail and its execution conditions in the direct Tool result only; the check stage keeps the no-output rule.
- A scope extension is self-served only under the same-directory rule: concrete files, in a directory that already holds a file of the enrolled scope, touching no risk-floor path. No count limit.
- Self-served additions are disclosed in the Review prompt from Kernel history; no TaskRecord field is added.
- The edit guard covers Host file-edit tools only and denies nothing when its entry store is unreadable.
- S4 makes three named contract changes and delivers a rule audit as a report that removes no rule.

## Testing strategy

Each acceptance names its test files and positive, negative and bound controls in the Spec's verification table. S2 starts with a characterization test of the current revision refusal. Contract-text acceptances are paired with a runtime acceptance for the same rule wherever a runtime form exists.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-1` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: the Executor reads the failed QA result. Then: it shows that prepare ran in an isolated delivery with a fresh home and no worktree node_modules, the declared timeout, and the last lines of the error output.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: the Executor needs src/events/index.ts and submits the revision. Then: it applies without a confirmation dialog.
- `SCN-3` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: the revision adds a file under a Kernel path, a new directory, or a glob. Then: it is refused as not compatible and the native confirmation remains the only way to apply it.
- `SCN-4` (Slice `S3`, automated): When: that session edits a file inside the active task's scope. Then: the edit is denied with the reason revision_owner_required and one recovery action.

## Out of scope

- Risk tiering and any decision-model use (tracked on #204).
- Reusing a host package cache in QA or raising the 600 s descriptor bound.
- Removing any rule the S4 audit lists.
- Intercepting shell writes in the S3 guard.

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: After this Slice alone, a QA prepare timeout or failure shows where and under which conditions it ran and the end of its error output.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: After this Slice alone, an Executor can add a sibling file to an enrolled scope through revise_intent with no confirmation dialog, and the Reviewer sees the addition. (blocked by: ceremony-trim-r647-s1-qa-prepare-diagnostics)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S3 --> **S3**: After this Slice alone, a session that entered the Planner cannot edit an executing task's files with a file-edit tool. (blocked by: ceremony-trim-r647-s2-scope-revision)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S4 --> **S4**: After this Slice alone, the Loop contract no longer carries the batch sections, and the Executor and Planner are no longer asked for the three unused texts. No user-visible change: only agent-facing contract text moves or shrinks. (blocked by: ceremony-trim-r647-s1-qa-prepare-diagnostics, ceremony-trim-r647-s3-revision-ownership)

title: Investigate batch-mode constraints on branches, worktrees and terminal tooling
body:
## Problem

Batch and Lane execution prescribe parts of the user's development setup. The planning principle agreed on 2026-10-12 is that the development environment belongs to the user and the Kernel constrains only what a task delivers. These rules were not examined against it yet:

- fixed branch names (`imm/<slug>`, `imm-lane/<slug>/<task>`) and one commit per child task
- any HEAD movement outside the Runner, other than a fast-forward, fails the batch
- the Runner neither removes worktrees nor branches; cleanup is left to the user
- the run contract carries operating steps for one specific terminal multiplexer
- an intent revision of one child task invalidates the whole batch plan (`plan_changed`)

## Wanted result

A report, not a change. For each rule above:

1. where it is enforced (runtime file and contract section)
2. which guarantee it protects, and whether that guarantee is about the delivery or about the environment
3. a recommendation: keep, make configurable, or remove, with the affected callers and tests

Changes follow as their own planned work after the report is reviewed.

## Ordering

Start after #219 lands, because that Slice moves the batch, Lane and terminal sections of the run contract into separate files.

## Out of scope

Review cost and `inspected_paths` (tracked in #177); the QA execution environment (Initiative candidate `host-owned-environment`).

title: [host-owned-env] Leave the development environment to the user
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=host-owned-environment -->

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

Several Kernel rules prescribe the user's development setup instead of the delivery. Deterministic QA copies the delivery into a disposable directory without installed dependencies, so every run reinstalls them. Command resolution reads '#!' lines and refuses tools reached through a version-manager shim. Staging-area state is checked on read-only status and at Enrollment, not only when a snapshot is frozen. The paths that force a higher risk are this repository's own paths, hard-coded for every project. Claude hooks append to the event log in sessions that have no managed work.

## Result

QA runs prepare and checks in the task's own working directory after an equality check against the frozen snapshot. A host tool behind a shim runs, and compound commands are written with sh -c. Status stays readable with unstaged files in scope, Enrollment can claim listed in-scope changes, and narrowing a scope needs no confirmation. Risk-floor paths come from a tracked project declaration and default to none. Hooks write nothing when the workspace has no active task or batch.

## Initiative design

Invariant: QA verifies exactly the frozen snapshot. Tracked content of the working directory inside the task scope must equal the snapshot tree before the first command and after each command; any difference fails the run and names the differing paths to the caller without storing them. Ignored files such as installed dependencies are the user's environment and take part in QA. Where QA runs is not prescribed: a worktree, the main checkout and a container are all valid. The prepare field stays in the descriptor and runs in place; null means no prepare.

Slices run strictly in series S1R, then S2 to S5 because each regenerates the same Claude bundle. S1R, which replaces the stopped S1, moves task QA in place and keeps the delivery copy only for the Lane batch integration recheck, whose merge candidate is never checked out. S2 stops interpreting '#!' lines and executes the resolved entry file directly. S3 moves staging checks to the freeze moment and lets the Enrollment confirmation claim listed in-scope changes; the index-flag refusal at freeze stays because S1 relies on it. S4 moves the risk floor out of the intent parser and reads it from a tracked declaration at .imm/risk-floor.json; a missing declaration means no floor, an invalid one makes every task critical, and the hash of an already enrolled intent must not change. S5 limits hook event-log writes to workspaces with active work.

Cross-Initiative ordering: S1 starts after the ceremony-trim Initiative (#215, last Slice #219) lands, because both change the same QA files and contract sections.

## Decisions

- QA location is the user's choice; task QA no longer builds its own copy of the delivery. The Lane batch integration recheck keeps the copy.
- prepare is kept and runs in place, so no descriptor version change is needed.
- No new descriptor field for shell commands: sh -c already works and is documented as the way to write a compound command.

## Current behavior

QA materializes the staged delivery into a temporary directory without ignored files, so dependencies are reinstalled on every run and tools bound to the project path may not work there.

## Desired behavior

Task QA runs in place. Tracked content inside the task scope must equal the frozen snapshot before the first command and after each command; a difference fails the run and returns the differing paths to the caller without storing them. Content outside the scope is not compared.

- the delivery materialization module (kept for the batch integration recheck only)
- run and Planner contract sections on where QA runs

- `HE-S1-A1`: In a real temporary Git repository a check that reads an ignored directory of the working directory passes, an in-scope tracked edit outside the frozen snapshot refuses before any command runs, a check that rewrites an in-scope tracked file fails as input drift, and an out-of-scope path may differ.
- `HE-S1-A2`: Both Hosts complete a passing task QA run with no delivery copy, the differing paths of a refused run are not stored, and aborting during a command still removes its processes.
- `HE-S1-A3`: The run and Planner contracts state the in-place rule and no longer describe task QA as running in a disposable delivery, ADR 0022 exists, and the generated Claude bundle matches the source.
