## Parent

| Initiative | `batch-resource-safety` |
| Parent Issue | [#309](https://github.com/dereknex/immune-brain/issues/309) |
| Slice | `S2` |
| Risk | `material` |

## Current behavior

Same-tick integration cleanup and redo use Git/Kernel facts but have no Executor process handle; completed-report rebuilding can omit cleanup observations.

## Desired behavior

Apply option A uniformly to both Hosts. Keep integrated Lanes, park destructive redo, preserve all contents, and distinguish delivery completion from cleanup. Do not substitute caller session state for proof.

## Key interfaces

- batch_lanes release/redo/revival transitions
- batch_worktrees Lane helpers versus detached verification
- batch_runner completedParentReport and existing report fields
- Lane lifecycle source/packaged contracts

## Acceptance criteria

- `AC1`: Retain Executor Lanes and real ignored data when exit is unproven, while ordinary integration and verified delivery still complete.
- `AC2`: Block destructive redo/revival, including missing-path recovery, without deleting resources or repeatedly consuming grants; independent siblings can continue.
- `AC3`: Keep retained-resource diagnostics visible through terminal replay and completed-report reconstruction without reenrolling delivered work.
- `AC4`: Align affected lifecycle contracts and mirrors with retention, preserve existing ownership/dialog protections, and document the owner and proof gate for future automation restoration.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-4` (automated, `AC1`): Actor: repository user. Given: a Child is integrated but its Executor is alive or unobserved. When: the batch advances. Then: its Lane and files remain; verified delivery may complete with a cleanup notice.
- `SCN-5` (automated, `AC2`): Actor: repository user. Given: a redo Lane contains an ignored user file and exit evidence is unavailable. When: redo or resume is requested. Then: it parks without destructive recreation or repeated grant spending.
- `SCN-6` (automated, `AC3`): Actor: repository user. Given: delivery completed with a retained Lane. When: the completed report is reopened. Then: it still reports the resource and does not reenroll the Child.

## Verification

Focused Parent/Lane, merge-queue, parked-revival, redo-slot, final-report, goal-driven report and contract/mirror tests. Use a fixture-owned live process and real ignored sentinel; no process-wide scanning.

## Blocked by

- `batch-resource-safety-s1`

## Out of scope

- Creating a trustworthy Host process observation provider
- Automatic cleanup/recreation restoration
- Broad terminal product routing changes
- Deleting user-owned external Lanes

## Agent handoff

Use docs/specs/batch-resource-safety-s2.spec.md. S1 is the prerequisite. The approved reduction intentionally retains resources and may pause redo. No blank receipt/caller boolean may authorize deletion. Preserve immutable evidence and existing record meanings; report any schema-changing requirement to Planner.

---

_Outbound visibility only: GitHub state never authorizes or settles work — Kernel TaskIntent, TaskRecord, QA, Review, and Assurance remain the execution authority. An Open Issue only means the Task still needs attention; only a claimless terminal projection closes it (`done` → Completed, `stopped` → Not planned)._

title: [Proposal] Spec↔code drift detection (EGM drift report)
body:
## Provenance

Borrowed from google/elephant-goldfish-model (`skills/egm_drift_report/SKILL.md`):
a design document is compared against current source, per document, and only
differences are reported. Adopted 2026-10-27 by Derek ("按建议采纳" on the EGM
borrow analysis, `~/workspace/your_files/immune-brain-egm-borrow-analysis-2026-10-27.md`,
item E4). This issue is the proposal; no code is written here.

## Problem

Immune-Brain verifies a point in time: the content-delivery predicate checks
scoped content equals the Review snapshot. There is no standing check for
whether the code still matches its Spec. Specs drift from code in both
directions:

- Forward: an implementation silently deviates from its Spec (a field never
  built, a dynamic rule hardcoded, a different pattern or library used).
- Reverse: code outgrows its Spec without the Spec being updated — scope creep
  no review round ever sees, because later reviews judge the diff against the
  current acceptance, not the original Spec.

## Design (from EGM, adapted)

Per Spec, an offline tool reads the Spec, locates the files and symbols it
names (search when the path is unclear, and prompt the author to add explicit
file links so the next detection is cheaper), reads current source, and
compares. Four drift classes:

1. Missing feature — the Spec has it, the code does not.
2. Incomplete model — a class or struct is missing a documented field.
3. Logic shortcut — what should be dynamic is hardcoded.
4. Architectural divergence — the implementation used a different pattern or
   library.

Report only differences: a clean Spec outputs exactly `No drift detected`,
never a description of the healthy parts. Reverse drift also counts — logic
present in code but mentioned in neither the Spec nor the README is reportable
drift. One dated report per run, one section per Spec, differences only. The
human decides whether to change the Spec or the code.

## Landing

New eval-tooling surface, next to #284 S1. It shares the S0 corpus idea
(committed Specs as the source of truth) and the S1 record-report shape
(a drift series in the record report: per-Spec drift counts by class), driven
by an offline tool that reads `docs/specs/*.spec.md`, extracts named
files/symbols, and compares against current code. Specs name the files they
govern with explicit paths — that naming convention is part of this issue.

## Sequencing and cadence

- Sequence: after #284 S1 lands, so this reuses the eval runner and the
  gold/silver labelling discipline instead of inventing a second one.
- Cadence (proposed, revisable when this issue is written): on-change,
  consistent with #284 D4 (eval runs on change, not on a schedule) — not
  EGM's weekly ritual.

## Acceptance

- An offline drift tool exists under eval tooling and runs against committed
  Specs without network or model calls.
- Its output is a dated report with one section per Spec, differences only,
  covering all four drift classes in both directions.
- The record report carries a per-Spec drift series by class.
- A Spec with no drift reports exactly `No drift detected`.

title: [Proposal] Knowledge-use eval: do executors actually use the guidance?
body:
## Provenance

From Thorsten Ball, “How I work with Agents” (X Article, 2026-10-25): knowledge
piles up in the codebase — AGENTS.md files, skills, scripts, docs — but do agents
actually use it? His answer is an experiment: spawn five blind agents, control
vs. treatment, and find out. Adopted 2026-10-27 by Derek (“都做” on the
Thorsten Ball follow-up). This issue is the proposal; no code is written here.

## Problem

#284's eval scores reviewer quality. Nothing scores whether executors actually
use the knowledge Immune-Brain keeps accumulating: BASELINE.md, the skill
contracts, the planning-quality-gate, the decision registry (when it exists).
The knowledge grows, but there is no measurement of whether it changes
outcomes. A rule nobody follows is indistinguishable from a rule that does not
exist — except it costs reading budget on every dispatch.

## Design (from Thorsten, adapted to the eval line)

A blind control-vs-treatment experiment over completed tasks, reusing the #284
S1 runner shape (offline, isolated checkouts, no live workflow state, no
TaskRecord created):

- **Treatment**: the executor runs with the guidance under test (a skill
  contract, a planning-quality-gate checklist, a BASELINE section).
- **Control**: the same task, the same frozen revision, the same acceptance —
  with that guidance withheld.
- **Blind**: the scorer does not know which arm produced the outcome.
- **Outcome**: rework rounds to pass, acceptance violations, and findings
  that the guidance exists to prevent. The question is never “did the agent
  quote the rule” but “did the outcome change”.

The experiment is an eval-tooling surface, not a workflow change: it runs
offline against the S0 corpus (or a purpose-built task sample), under the
project's existing research/model channel authorization, stated in the run
report. Withholding guidance from the control arm is legitimate here because
nothing ships from the experiment — it is measurement, not execution.

## Landing

New eval-tooling surface next to #284 S1. It shares the S1 runner (`scripts/review-eval/run.ts` shape) and the record-report format, but it is
a second eval line, not an S1 item: S1 scores reviewer quality per gold case;
this scores guidance effectiveness per task. Candidate homes, in order:
(1) an extension of the S1 runner with a guidance arm, if the runner's
configuration shape admits it; (2) a sibling script under `scripts/review-eval/`.

## Sequencing and cadence

- Sequence: after #284 S1 lands, so this reuses the runner and the gold/silver
  labelling discipline instead of inventing a second one.
- Cadence: on-change, consistent with #284 D4 (eval runs on change, not on a
  schedule). A natural trigger is any change to the guidance under test: when
  a skill contract or gate checklist changes, the experiment answers whether
  the change mattered.

## Acceptance

- An offline experiment exists that replays a task sample with a guidance arm
  and a control arm, blind-scored, with no live workflow effect.
- Its report states, per guidance under test: rework rounds, acceptance
  violations, and prevented-finding counts for both arms, with the delta.
- Guidance with no measurable outcome delta is reported as such — the
  experiment may conclude a rule is dead weight, and that is a result, not
  a failure.
- The corpus and scoring rules are pinned per run so a later run can be
  compared; a run that cannot be compared says so instead of presenting a
  delta.

title: [Proposal] Skill rename round 2: bare verbs
body:
# [Proposal] Skill rename round 2: bare verbs

## Provenance

- Follows #163 (round 1, closed 2026-10-09): `imm-loop` → `imm-run`, `imm-agent-doc-maintain` → `imm-doc-slim`, `imm-review-retro` → `imm-retro`. That round kept the `imm-` prefix as a namespace.
- 2026-10-27 Derek reopened the rename: first design-driven (names from each skill's design, not just shortening), then the 4-char prefix question (surveyed mattpocock/skills, pstack, EGM naming), then all-verbs style. This proposal records the final set Derek approved on 2026-10-28. The batch follows this issue.

## Mapping (old → new)

| Old | New | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `imm-brainstorm` | `clarify` | The trigger's first word ("clarify or explore requirements"); the user's intent when invoking; plain verb. `frame` was the design term but has noun/verb ambiguity; `brainstorm` names the method, not the act. |
| `imm-planner` | `draw-up` | "Draw up a plan / spec / contract" is the collocation for drafting authoritative documents; covers both deliverables. `bind` named only the binding mechanism, not making spec + plan. `plan` collides with `/plan` on both hosts (see below). `define` was the runner-up. |
| `imm-run` | `drive` | The loop is the essence (its contract title is still "Loop"); coordination through review to settlement. `settle` names only the terminal act. |
| `imm-retro` | `revisit` | Re-examine past work to find problems: review + retrospective in one verb. `rank` named only the ranking output, not the retrospective main responsibility. `retrospective` is a noun. Bare `retro` collides with mattpocock/skills' `retro` on Pi (see below). |
| `imm-doc-slim` | `slim` | The established term, already a verb; the operation distinguishes it from the prunes. |
| `imm-doc-prune` | `prune-docs` | The two prunes share a verb, so the object is required; verb-first under all-verbs. |
| `imm-test-prune` | `prune-tests` | Same. |
| `imm-pr-fix` | `fix-pr` | Bare `fix` says nothing; verb-first. |

## Style principles

- **All verbs**, like `clarify`. Pipeline reads `clarify → draw-up → drive`.
- **Name = distinguishing information.** Managed skills share one object (the task), so the verb distinguishes them; standalone skills have different objects, so the object is part of the name where the verb alone is ambiguous (`prune-docs` vs `prune-tests`, `fix-pr`).
- **No `imm-` prefix (scheme A).** On Claude Code the plugin name is the namespace (`/immune-brain:<skill>`), so the prefix is redundant there. On Pi there is no plugin namespace, so the names rely on distinctiveness instead (see collision checks).
- **No aliases.** The existing contract stands: no alias, feature flag, or second public surface. Breaking change, direct, no deprecation, with this breaking note.

## Host conflicts (verified)

- `plan`: Claude Code built-in `/plan` (enter plan mode; `plan` is also a permission mode and a built-in subagent type); Pi built-in `/plan` (`packages/coding-agent/src/slash-commands/builtin-registry.ts`, toggle plan mode). A skill named `plan` would be confused with the hosts' own plan mode on both hosts.
- `run`: Claude Code built-in `/run`.
- `review`: Claude Code built-in `/review`, and Review is immune-brain's own authority concept (reviewer / verifier); the word is reserved.
- Pi skill loading has no plugin namespace: all skills load into one map keyed by bare name, first loaded wins, the loser only gets a collision diagnostic and is not loaded (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts`, `loadSkills`). Claude Code namespaces plugin skills as `/immune-brain:<skill>`.
- Pi name rule: lowercase `a-z`, `0-9`, hyphens only, max 64 chars. All new names comply.

## Upstream collision checks

Every candidate was grepped against the full skill-name lists of mattpocock/skills and pstack (clones, 2026-10-27/28). All clean, except bare `retro` — mattpocock/skills has `engineering/retro` — which is why `revisit` was chosen over `retro`. EGM keeps its own `egm_` prefix, so no bare collision. Note pstack and mattpocock/skills already collide with each other on bare `tdd` and `teach`; bare-name collision is an accepted risk in the ecosystem, resolved by host precedence — mitigated here by distinctive words.

## Execution scope

Rename, in one batch:

- 8 skill directories under `plugins/immune-brain/skills/` + `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name:` + H1 titles.
- `dist/*.md` files (`dist/imm-*.md` → new names, including `dist/imm-run-batch.md` → `dist/drive-batch.md`) + all cross-references.
- README skill table, `skill-registry-consistency` test (hardcodes the 8 names), runtime references, skills guide.
- Skills guide gains a naming checklist (see below).
- Also fixes the leftover `# Immune-Brain: Loop` title in `imm-run`'s `SKILL.md` (never updated in round 1).

Also in scope per **Decisions** below: run-entry gate recognition rules, ADR 0031, major changeset, current-surface allowlist test. Docs scope is current surface only (see **Verification (revised)**).

Not touched: `bin/imm-kernel`, `bin/imm-plan`, `.imm/`, plugin name `immune-brain`, `.pi-extension` extension names. Version bump at release time (breaking change).

## Naming checklist (new rule for the skills guide)

A new skill name must pass four checks: (1) not a Claude Code built-in command, (2) not a Pi built-in command, (3) not an existing skill name in mattpocock/skills, pstack, or EGM, (4) not another skill name in this plugin. This rule exists because `plan` failed checks (1) and (2) after being proposed.

## Verification

> Superseded by **Verification (revised)** below.

- `bun scripts/sync-dist-docs.ts --check` shows 0 drift.
- Full test suite passes.
- No remaining `imm-<old-name>` strings outside `.imm/` history and binaries.
- Model routing is unaffected (routing reads descriptions, not names; every description keeps its "Immune-Brain" mention).

## Decisions (grilling 2026-10-28)

- Rename scope: skill names, registry `next_actions`/`title`, H1 (`Immune-Brain: <Verb>`). Unchanged: `role`, phase enum `plan|run`, artifact names, domain terms (Planner, Loop).
- Run-entry gate (`runtime/assurance/phase_entry.ts`, `runtime/claude/lane_guard.ts`, Pi `imm-canary-work.ts`):
  - Recognizes the new names bare, `immune-brain:`-prefixed and `skill:`-prefixed.
  - A same-named user/project command is parsed as an alias; a same-named user/project skill makes the bare form not mint an entry token (prefixed forms still mint). Both Hosts.
  - Alias bodies match only marked mentions (`/drive`, `immune-brain:drive`, `skill:drive`), never bare prose words.
  - Old names, including `imm-loop`, are no longer recognized anywhere.
- New ADR 0031 records the rename and the entry-recognition rules; it amends ADR 0025's recognition part. Accepted ADRs stay unedited.
- Naming checklist gains check (5): no same-named local user skill or command.
- Release: major changeset (6.0.0) with breaking note: old→new table, update user aliases by hand, refresh the Claude Code plugin cache / Pi `/reload`, prefixed entry forms.
- Execution: one Managed task under `imm-run`, no Lanes; settle before merge; first post-merge run smoke-tests `/drive`.

## Verification (revised)

- Replaces "no remaining `imm-<old-name>` strings outside `.imm/`". An allowlist test asserts zero old names in: `plugins/immune-brain/**`, root `README.md`/`CONTEXT.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/agents/**`, `docs/reference/**`, `docs/user_manual.md`, `tests/**` (fixture filenames included). Dated history stays unedited (plans, specs incl. unarchived, ADRs, reports, solutions, brainstorms, evidence, archives, proposals, benchmark-results, CHANGELOG, existing changesets, `.imm/`); `CONTEXT.md` gains an old→new mapping table.
- `bun scripts/sync-dist-docs.ts --check` shows 0 drift; `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass.
- Gate tests cover: bare/prefixed new names mint; old names and `imm-loop` do not; alias-body prose such as "drive the build" does not; a same-named user skill blocks the bare form only.

title: Initiative amendment drops multi-line historical Slice entries, losing their prerequisite annotation
body:
## Problem

An Initiative amendment drops the continuation lines of a historical Slice entry whose result spans more than one line. When the dropped text carries the entry's `(blocked by: …)` annotation, the rewritten Parent no longer declares that Slice's prerequisites.

- `baselineHistoricalSlices` (`plugins/immune-brain/runtime/github_issue_tracker.ts:1412-1443`) collects historical entries with `/^.*?<!-- immune-brain:slice-id=… -->.*$/gm`. `.` does not match a newline, so each carried entry is only its marker line (`lines.push(line)`, `:1434`).
- A Slice entry can span lines: `slices[].result` and `goal` pass through `projectionText` → `publicText` (`:341-346`, `:1778-1783`), which rejects only `\0`. `createInitiativeBody` (`:1214`) renders `- [ ] <marker> **S**: <result>` and appends ` (blocked by: …)` after the whole result text. A result containing a newline therefore puts the annotation on a later line.
- The amended Parent is rebuilt from `historicalSlices` (`:1382`), so the continuation lines, including the annotation, are removed from the published plan.

Since `d03982c` (#285), isolated GitHub Enrollment reads prerequisites from the Parent Slice entry, scanning from the marker line to the next Slice marker. An entry stripped of its annotation therefore reads as having no prerequisites, so an amendment can re-open the bypass #285 closed. This also breaks the tracker contract in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` ("Existing Initiative amendment"): "the Parent keeps every historical Slice entry exactly once". Only the marker line is kept.

Evidence status: confirmed by reading the code at the lines cited above. No runtime reproduction yet.

## What correct looks like

An amendment carries each historical Slice entry byte-for-byte. The entry is the full text from its marker line to the next Slice marker or the end of the Slices list, which is the same boundary `assertIsolatedTaskPrerequisites` uses. A historical entry the amendment cannot delimit unambiguously fails closed with a structured result and no remote write.

Optionally, and separately, publication could reject or normalize newlines in `slices[].result` / `goal`. That does not repair Parents that are already published, so it does not replace the fix above.

## Acceptance

- Fixture: a baseline Parent with a historical Slice whose result spans lines and whose `(blocked by: T-a)` annotation is on a continuation line. After amendment, the Parent body contains that entry byte-identical to the baseline, and `assertIsolatedTaskPrerequisites` for that Slice still rejects while T-a is unsettled.
- Fixture: single-line historical entries. The amended Parent body is byte-identical to today's output.
- Fixture: a historical entry whose continuation text contains another Slice's marker, or that cannot be delimited. The amendment returns a structured failure with zero mutations.
- `bun scripts/build-claude-plugin.ts --check` passes, and a `patch` changeset is added.

## Out of scope

- The prerequisite parsing in `assertIsolatedTaskPrerequisites` (landed in #285).
- The GitHub batch plan projection, which is still edge-derived (#285 `BR-DEFER-1`).

title: [Proposal] Revisit refactor: workflow-health retro (model-load ranking removed)
body:
## Provenance

`revisit` today answers "model load" (ranking of models by cross-model review load from Pi session logs), not "workflow health". A 2026-10-29 review of the skill (contract `dist/revisit.md`, analyzer `skills/revisit/scripts/review_retro.ts`, fixtures, and the #284 S1 design) found it unfit as immune-brain's own retrospective: no closed loop, no trend, no cadence, and blind to the acceptance-anchored loops that matter most. Upstream checks found loop-closing methods worth borrowing (pstack `correct`, `reflect`) but no upstream trend, cadence, acceptance-anchoring, or reviewer-quality-ground-truth solution — those are immune-brain's own work, centered on #284 S1.

## Decisions already made (Derek, 2026-10-29)

1. **Positioning: (b), refined.** `revisit` becomes the workflow-health retro. Model load is removed from scope; workflow health is the sole focus.
2. **~~Guardrail (D2 stands).~~ Superseded 2026-10-30 by D2-partial below.** Original text: `revisit` references #284 S1's metrics; it never recomputes record-based metrics. D2 (adopted 2026-10-20, keep the `imm-retro` boundary, record-based quality metrics live in the eval tooling) is not reversed by this refactor.
3. **Model dimension vs model load.** Removing "model load" (whose edits triggered how much review) does not remove the model dimension: S1 item 9's per-model breakdown is reviewer effectiveness (recall, FP rate, rounds-to-pass by reviewer model) — a workflow-health signal, kept.
4. **No new skill.** pstack `correct` and `reflect` enter as methods inside revisit's follow-through section, not as new skills. A standalone `/correct`-style skill is a separate later decision.

## Decisions (Derek, 2026-10-30, grilling session)

1. **Absorb `workflow-evidence-retro` now (D2-partial).** The project-local `.agents/skills/workflow-evidence-retro` (audit-record workflow retro; used for `docs/reports/workflow-evidence-baseline.md` and `rework-root-causes-2026-10-08.md`) merges into `revisit` and is then deleted. Its §1 sampling and §2 counts become analyzer code with fixtures; its §3–4 method (read all findings, cross-boundary trace, counterchecks, historical ≠ current, one smallest improvement) becomes the follow-through section of `dist/revisit.md`, alongside pstack `correct`'s fix ladder.
2. **D2 partially reversed (ADR required).** `revisit` may read **committed** `.imm/audit/**` only — never live `.imm/` state, SQLite, or the authority store — and only when `--audit <project-root>` names one project (no default scan, no cross-project scan). Parsing and proof checking go through the kernel's `readAuditTaskPair` (`plugins/immune-brain/runtime/kernel/storage.ts`), not a second implementation. `revisit` computes only the lifecycle counts #284 S1 does not cover: QA execution failures, intent revisions (compatible/breaking), user-authorized rework, stop events, evidence bindings. Review-quality metrics (S1 items 3/7/8/9) stay with #284 S1's eval tooling; `revisit` references them. The ADR marks D2 in `docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md` as superseded-by; #284's TaskIntents are not revised.
3. **Ranking removed outright.** The model-load ranking table and its tests retire in the first slice, with the retirement stated. The `pass%` question is moot. Contract tests for surviving signals stay green and are not weakened.
4. **Session unit stays per file.** Pi stores `sessions/<cwd-slug>/<file>.jsonl`; each file carries its own `{"type":"session","id":...}` header, and a directory holds many independent sessions of one cwd (up to 388 observed). Merging a directory would join unrelated sessions. Replace the directory-merge item with a read-only check for cross-file parent/fork links; only if such links exist, stitch by link.
5. **Pending decisions resolved:** snapshots only to an explicit `--out <dir>` (no default; absent → stdout only); Claude Code reader out of scope this round (counter stays reader-agnostic); follow-through is report-only with copy-ready TaskIntent/issue drafts; cadence is a manual monthly run + reminder (no cron/daemon, Boundary unchanged on that point).
6. **Name unchanged.** The skill stays `revisit`; description becomes a workflow-health retro over session logs and committed audit records; model-ranking triggers are removed.
7. **Two ADRs, one per boundary step:** D2-partial lands with the audit reader slice; snapshot writes land with the snapshot slice.
8. **Audit is the primary source; Pi sessions are optional (2026-10-30, follow-up).** A read-only survey of committed audit (main HEAD: 287 task records — v4 208, v3 9, v2 70; 2026-09-01..10-28) shows v4 records carry every WER §2 count and structured findings (`acceptance_id`, `review_round`, `anchor`, `summary`, `evidence`), so lifecycle counts, raw review counts and repeat-finding grouping come from audit, not session text (scope of the review counts: decision 11). Sessions add only what audit lacks: non-Managed work, token/cost (`usage` in Pi messages), infra jitter that never became a finding, and per-model reviewer data until S1 item 9 records reviewer model (audit `actor_id` is role-level only). Pi session input moves behind `--sessions`; Claude Code reader stays out.
9. **Audit reads the HEAD git tree.** `--audit <root>` exports `.imm/audit/**` from the root's HEAD (`git archive`) into a temporary directory and reads it with `readAuditTaskPair(<tmpdir>, ...)` (which reads disk paths under its root), never working-tree files; the report header names the HEAD hash and the terminal-sample bias (only merged terminal runs; unmerged Lane branches, non-terminal runs and stopped runs whose pair was never committed are absent). A `--audit-ref` multi-ref mode is later work. Known gap, not fixed by revisit: whether every stopped run's audit pair is committed is unverified (kernel/batch guarantee).
10. **Author attribution survives ranking removal.** S1 removes the ranking table and its computation/output only; author model stays a field on edit events, because #284 RVE-S1 (`docs/plans/review-verifier-eval-s1-metrics.intent.json`) splits blocking `violated.kind` per author model. RVE-S1 and this Initiative both touch `review_retro.ts` and its tests, so their slices run serially.
11. **Raw review counts only; derived review metrics stay with #284 S1 (2026-10-30).** S2's per-run sample table lists WER §2's raw counts from audit: review rework events (`request_rework` by review authority), review pass attestations, findings by source/status. `revisit` computes no median, p95, share, rounds-to-pass or per-acceptance series — those stay RVE-S1 items 3/7 (`docs/plans/review-verifier-eval-s1-metrics.intent.json`, unchanged). Boundary: raw counts vs distributions/rates/series. Session-side `rounds/task` stays as a weak supplementary signal behind `--sessions`. Corrects decision 8's earlier wording ("rounds/task, per-acceptance series from audit"), which overlapped D2-partial.

### Slices

| Slice | Content | This round |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | Ranking removal (author field kept), epoch timestamps + skipped count, `--exclude`, session-unit check, Pi input behind `--sessions`, description/Invocation rewrite | enroll |
| S2 | Audit reader over the HEAD git tree via `readAuditTaskPair` (primary: lifecycle counts, raw per-run review counts per decision 11, sample-bias header) + D2-partial ADR | enroll |
| S3 | Follow-through section grouped from audit findings (`acceptance_id`/`anchor`; sessions supplementary), report-only drafts + retire `workflow-evidence-retro` (move `tests/rework-root-cause-contract.test.ts` retro assertions to `dist/revisit.md`; update `docs/reports/workflow-evidence-baseline.md` entry link; keep the baseline as a historical example) | enroll |
| S4 | Snapshot pair + diff mode + snapshot ADR | Spec only |
| — | S1 record-report consumer (interface stub only), Claude Code reader, scheduled cadence | not planned |

## Refactor shape: four layers

Today input, analysis, output, and memory are fused in one analyzer plus a stdout report. The refactor separates them:

1. **Inputs (collectors).** Each source has a reader emitting normalized retro events (review executed, edit, verdict, finding, registration). The Pi reader exists; a Claude Code reader and an S1 record-report consumer are new. Test strategy unchanged: one fixture set per reader, counter tested on synthetic events.
2. **Analysis (counter).** Sees only normalized events, never log formats. This is what makes a Claude Code reader a new reader instead of a rewrite, and S1 access a new reader instead of a metric change.
3. **Memory (snapshots).** Each run stores a snapshot plus a decision record; a diff mode compares snapshots. Snapshot format follows pstack `show-me-your-work`: machine-readable counters plus decision rows with evidence pointers — so a diff shows why things changed, not just that numbers moved.
4. **Action (follow-through emission).** The report gains a "candidate improvements" section. `revisit` stays read-only: it emits, it does not execute. The loop is closed by whoever disposes of the emission (the user or a Managed task).

## Phases (suggested order)

### Phase 1: make the surviving instrument honest (no boundary change)

Superseded in part 2026-10-30 (decision 8): session-side `rounds/task` decontamination is no longer worth heavy investment — audit supplies rounds/task. Keep only the session fixes listed for S1 in the slice table.

Note: since the ranking table becomes legacy, its ranking-specific fixes are dropped. Fix only what survives as workflow-health signals:

- Finding classification groundwork (repeat-finding summaries across sessions — the input `correct` consumes).
- `rounds/task` decontamination (exclude canary/QA harness re-registration; `--exclude` flag symmetric with `--project`).
- ~~Session unit from file to directory~~ (superseded 2026-10-30, decision 4): keep one file = one session; add a read-only check for cross-file parent/fork links and stitch only by link if any exist.
- Timestamps parsed to epoch, not string-compared; timestamp-less/malformed lines counted in the header's skipped number instead of silently dropped.
- The `pass%` doc/code mismatch (contract says a `[VERDICT:]` tag judges without a contract; code requires `[SCORE:]` for the tag path) is moot if the ranking table goes; if any judged-share column survives, resolve it one way or the other with a test.
- Existing contract tests stay green; new fixtures only added, never rewriting old ones.

### Phase 2: follow-through emission (no boundary change)

Updated 2026-10-30 (decision 8): grouping input is audit findings (`acceptance_id`, `anchor`, `summary`); session repeats are supplementary.

The report's "candidate improvements" section. Each item carries: class (correct's method — repeated findings grouped by summary pattern; by `violated.kind` once S1 items 3–4 land), evidence (counts + example sessions), suggested level (correct's ladder: architecture > types > lint > test > docs last), and suggested disposition (TaskIntent draft / doc change / S1 metric). Skill-change proposals pass through reflect's approval gate: explicit user approval before any skill file moves, and any change passes the contract tests plus `sync-dist-docs.ts --check`.

### Phase 3: memory and trend (needs a boundary decision)

- Snapshot pair per run: `snapshot-<date>.json` (all counters, diff-computable) + `decisions-<date>.tsv` (show-me-your-work rows, one candidate improvement per row with an evidence pointer).
- A diff mode comparing two snapshots.
- Location: a user-specified reports directory — not `.imm/`, not session logs. Snapshots are small; keep all.
- This extends the Boundary section (today: "does not persist snapshots"). It is a boundary extension, not a D2 reversal, and needs to be recorded as such (spec/ADR).

### Phase 4: input expansion (two items, different dependencies)

- Claude Code reader — only if the Claude Code scope decision lands. Pi and Claude Code numbers must not merge into one ranking; host stays a dimension column (different schemas, different coverage).
- S1 record-report consumer — after S1 enrolls. Until then, only the interface is defined (input format, reference mode, D2 guardrail); no numbers are hardcoded into the report.

### Phase 5: cadence (blocked on log location, decide location first)

Suggested monthly (a retro's cadence; weekly is the upstream/field-watch rhythm). Three location options: (a) manual monthly run + reminder (weakest); (b) a scheduled task on the user's Pi host (how its output reaches chat TBD); (c) session logs synced to the VM, then a VM cron runs the analyzer (the only fully automated option, needs sync setup). Location before cadence — not the reverse.

## Guardrails (what the refactor must not do)

- Never compute record-based **review-quality** metrics (those stay with #284 S1); lifecycle counts from committed audit records only, per D2-partial (2026-10-30). Never create TaskIntents, issues, or commits (Kernel authority; #251: Git is a user-owned carrier, not delivery authority).
- No hard gates. `revisit` reports; it does not gate (the Guard's no-hard-thresholds stance).
- No big-bang analyzer rewrite. The analyzer is 380 lines with good tests; Phase 1 moves in small steps.
- No merged Pi/Claude Code ranking (host is a dimension).
- No hardcoded numbers before S1 exists (interface stub only).

## Dependencies

- **#284 S1 (blocking for the main content).** Workflow-health content is mostly S1 metrics: per-acceptance repeat-count series (item 7), review timing (item 8), per-model breakdown (item 9), verifier performance (S2/S3). Until S1 enrolls, the retro's workflow-health signals are thin (session logs offer only `rounds/task`, finding-repeat summaries, and similar thin signals) — the stub period is the main risk. S1 enrollment is itself gated on the 30 gold labels (D5, Derek).
- **S1 items 3–4** (session-visible metrics into the retro analyzer: blocking by `violated.kind`, disposition counts) are already planned inside the current boundary and land with S1.

## Pending decisions (for the planner) — all resolved 2026-10-30, see Decisions above

1. Snapshot location + whether scheduled runs are allowed (boundary extension).
2. Claude Code in or out of scope.
3. Follow-through emission: report-only, or may it file proposal issues (the latter is a boundary question).
4. Cadence location: manual / Pi-host schedule / synced-logs cron.
5. Phase 1's `pass%` resolution, if any judged-share column survives.

## Relation to other issues

- #284 owns the metrics this refactor references; this issue must not duplicate S1's computation.
- #316 (drift report) and #317 (knowledge-use eval) are adjacent proposals, not parts of this refactor.

## Provenance

- Derived from #322: the originating feature Issue for this Initiative.

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

revisit ranks models by how much review their edits triggered, which no longer answers a question we act on. Its session-log numbers are noisy (string timestamp comparison, harness re-registration in rounds/task). Workflow-friction analysis of terminal runs lives in a separate project-local Skill, workflow-evidence-retro, that duplicates the method and is not shipped.

## Result

revisit reports workflow health: lifecycle and raw review counts per committed terminal run read from one project's HEAD Git tree, a sample-bias header, and a candidate-improvements evidence section, with Pi sessions as an optional supplement. The model-load ranking and workflow-evidence-retro are retired. revisit stays read-only and report-only.

## Initiative design

Spec: docs/specs/revisit-workflow-health.spec.md. Layers: reader (Pi sessions; committed audit) -> per-event or per-run rows -> counter -> report. Audit parsing and proof checking stay in the Kernel: the audit reader exports .imm/audit/** from HEAD with git archive into a temporary directory and calls readAuditTaskPair; it never reads working-tree audit files, live .imm/ state, SQLite or the authority store. revisit counts lifecycle and raw review events only; derived review metrics (rounds-to-pass median/p95, shares, per-acceptance series, per-model breakdown) stay with #284 RVE-S1. Author model stays a session event field for RVE-S1. Slices run serially S1 -> S2 -> S3 (shared review_retro.ts, dist/revisit.md and Spec); RVE-S1 also edits review_retro.ts and must not run in the same batch as any of them. ADR 0032 records the D2-partial boundary with S2.

## Decisions

- #322 decisions 1-11 (2026-10-30): absorb workflow-evidence-retro; D2 partially reversed for committed audit at HEAD only; ranking removed; one file = one session; report-only; Claude Code reader out; audit primary, sessions optional; raw counts only.
- Session-unit check closed in planning: all 417 immune-brain Pi session headers carry only cwd,id,timestamp,type,version, so no stitching is built.
- The review-verifier-eval Spec D2 note was written in planning, not by S2, so RVE-S1's Spec binding is not disturbed during execution.

## Testing strategy

Focused bun tests per Slice: tests/review-retro-analyzer.test.ts drives run() over committed session fixtures; tests/review-retro-audit.test.ts builds temporary Git repositories from copied real audit pairs to prove HEAD-only reads, proof-mismatch and incomplete-pair skips, and v2 '-' fields; tests/rework-root-cause-contract.test.ts pins the absorbed method text in dist/revisit.md.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-1` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: they run /revisit 30. Then: the report shows usage, rounds/task over kept tasks, finding totals and a skipped-line count, and no model ranking.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: they run /revisit 30 --audit .. Then: the report shows per-run lifecycle and raw review counts from HEAD, with the HEAD commit and the sample-bias line in its header.
- `SCN-3` (Slice `S3`, automated): When: they run /revisit 30 --audit .. Then: the report lists repeat groups with run pointers, jitter separately, and per-round acceptance ids for high-round runs.
- `SCN-4` (Slice `S3`, manual): When: the agent follows the revisit follow-through method. Then: the write-up names at most three opportunities with evidence and counterchecks and one smallest improvement with a copy-ready draft.

## Out of scope

- S4 snapshot and diff (--out <dir>, snapshot/decisions files, diff mode, its own ADR): Spec follow-up, a later Initiative.
- --audit-ref multi-ref reads during a batch.
- Claude Code session reader.
- Guaranteeing that every stopped run's audit pair is committed (Kernel/batch concern).
- Any change to #284 RVE-S1's TaskIntent or its derived metrics.

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: revisit's session report shows workflow-health signals only, with honest timestamp handling and --exclude.

title: [Proposal] Lane preferences: one preset, default is the current host config
body:
## Note

This proposal supersedes the layered design originally filed here (env vars, repo-level named profiles, a six-layer stack, a resolver helper, and a recording extension), and refines the simplification that followed it. Per Derek's 2026-10-30 direction — unify to one preset + default = current host config, remove the other schemes, as simple as possible — with profiles inside the preset file, and the decisions settled in the 2026-10-30 grilling session (see the latest comment). Earlier texts are preserved in the issue history and in the follow-up comments.

## Problem

Lane preferences today live only as prose directives in a tracked instruction file (`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, `## Immune-Brain Preferences`): `Lane max parallel`, `Lane Executor Host`, `Lane Executor model`, `Lane Executor effort`, plus `Batch final verification`. One shared file serves the whole team, so personal choices (a different model, a different host, lower parallelism on a weaker laptop) and temporary choices (try another model for one batch) both require editing the file and committing, then reverting. The user-level file does not fix it: a repo directive overrides it, and it cannot vary per project.

## Design: one preset file, profiles inside it, default is the current host config

### Default: the current host config (nothing set)

When no preset file exists, or it has no `active` field, behavior is today's "without it" column, with zero configuration:

- No `max_parallel`: one Lane at a time (a batch stays serial unless the request asks for lanes).
- Host: the Parent's own Host type, else the other allowlisted Host.
- Model and effort: the Executor Host's own defaults.

### Preset: one optional file, never committed, holding named profiles

```json
{
  "active": "fast",
  "profiles": {
    "fast": {"max_parallel": 8, "executor_host": "claude-code", "executor_model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "executor_effort": "high"},
    "cheap": {"max_parallel": 2}
  }
}
```

- Path: `.imm/lanes.local.json`, gitignored with one `.gitignore` line. One clone, one person, never committed. No other file carries lane config.
- The file has exactly two top-level keys: `active` (optional) and `profiles`. There is no `contract` field: no program reads this file; the Parent reads it directly.
- `profiles` maps names to configurations. Each profile has four optional fields: `max_parallel`, `executor_host`, `executor_model`, `executor_effort`. Anything a profile does not name falls back to the default above.
- `active` names the profile in effect. No `active` field means the default above, even if profiles are defined.
- A profile's `max_parallel` turns lane mode on, as today.
- A profile's model/effort apply only when the same profile also names the host; otherwise they are reported and not applied (a model id belongs to one Host). They are never applied to the default-resolved host.
- The Parent reads the file only from its own checkout root. The batch runner and Lane worktrees read none of these values.

### Errors are reported, never guessed

Malformed JSON, an unknown profile name (in `active` or in a request), an unknown key (top-level or inside a profile, e.g. a misspelled `executor_modle`), or an invalid value (non-positive `max_parallel`, a host outside `pi`/`claude-code`) is reported, and the batch is not started on guessed or default values.

### Request instruction overrides per batch, field by field

For one batch, the request may name a profile (otherwise `active` applies), and may state explicit field values that overlay the selected profile field by field — e.g. "use `cheap`, but max parallel 3". Nothing is written to the file.

### Unchanged from today

- The Parent resolves before the first `start_unattended_batch` call; the batch runner reads none of these values.
- After resolving, the Parent displays one non-blocking line with each selected value and its per-field source (`request` / `preset:<profile>` / `default`).
- On resume, the recorded `max_parallel` stands, as today. No new recording machinery.

## Batch final verification

The `Batch final verification` directive is removed. The `final_verification` runtime parameter is unchanged. Its commands resolve in this order:

1. commands stated literally in the current request;
2. the full test suite and type-check commands the repository instruction file names in prose (e.g. "uses `bun test`; type checking is `bun run typecheck`");
3. none — the completion report says nothing was run.

The constraints (plain commands without shell syntax or quoting, at most 8) move to the `final_verification` parameter's description, independent of source. The Parent never invents a command the repository does not name.

## Removed

- Environment variables (`IMM_LANE_*`), the six-layer stack, the resolver helper, and the batch-record recording extension.
- Repo and user-level instruction-file lane directives (`Lane max parallel`, `Lane Executor Host`, `Lane Executor model`, `Lane Executor effort`): they stop being read. Profiles exist only inside the personal preset file.
- The `Batch final verification` directive (see above).
- Other preferences (e.g. `Initiative carrier default`) stay in instruction files, unchanged.

## Documentation

- A new ADR records the exception: lane preferences are a personal, per-clone, gitignored JSON file, while every other preference stays in Host instruction files. It states its relation to ADR 0013 (optional parallel batch lanes).
- `docs/reference/immune-brain-config.md`: the opening principle ("does not load an agent-local … file") names this exception; the Lane Preferences section is rewritten.
- `drive-batch` Lane Preferences is rewritten in its source and the dist mirror resynced.
- CHANGELOG gets a breaking entry naming both removals and the migration.

## Migration (one-time, breaking for existing setups)

Anyone relying on repo or user-level lane directives copies those values once into a profile in their preset file (and names it `active`), or deletes them and uses the default. Anyone relying on `Batch final verification` names the commands in instruction-file prose or in the request. There is no automatic migration. This repository's own `AGENTS.md` lane lines (`Lane max parallel` … `Lane Executor effort`) are deleted; `Initiative carrier default` stays.

## Delivery

One TaskIntent: drive-batch source + dist mirror, config reference, new ADR, `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, CHANGELOG, and the directive-table assertions in `tests/role-prompt-bridge.test.ts`. Creating a maintainer's local preset file is outside its scope.

## Acceptance

- No preset file, or no `active` field: behavior is exactly today's default column (serial unless requested, Parent's own Host type, host defaults).
- `active` names a profile: its named fields apply, unnamed fields fall back to the current host config.
- Request names a profile: that profile applies for that batch only; request field values overlay it field by field.
- Profile model/effort without a profile host: reported, not applied.
- Unknown profile name, unknown key, malformed JSON, or invalid value: reported, batch not started.
- The preset file is gitignored; no lane directives and no `Batch final verification` directive remain in tracked instruction files or in the documented directive table.
- Final verification resolves request → repository prose → none, with the ≤8 / no-shell-syntax constraints on the parameter.
- Display line shows each value + per-field source (`request` / `preset:<profile>` / `default`).
- New ADR, config reference exception, and CHANGELOG breaking entry exist.

title: [Proposal] Revisit follow-up: evidence-chain diagnosis instead of a statistics report
body:
## Provenance

Follow-up to #322 (S1–S3 merged, `87f7f62`). On 2026-10-30 a `/revisit` run answered "where does the workflow make people step in, and what should change first?" with tool counts and `rounds/task`. Under follow-up questions the agent wrote ad-hoc JSONL scans with inconsistent windows and session definitions, and a helper investigation spent about 11 minutes producing results that still needed checking. Some errors broke rules the contract already states (inferring the rounds distribution from a mean, treating tool calls as human confirmations, reading `request_stop` as an abandoned run without its result). The structural cause is that the normal path gives counts while the question asks for causes.

## Problem (verified)

- The session reader skips every non-assistant line (`plugins/immune-brain/skills/revisit/scripts/review_retro.ts`, `m.role !== "assistant"`). User input and tool results are never read, so stop → result → user action → recovery chains cannot be rebuilt from analyzer output.
- `SessionEvent` carries `author`/`key`/`taskId`/`summary` only: no timestamp, line, message id, `toolCallId`, run id, or call↔result link. A reader cannot jump from a number to its source line.
- `submit_review` usually omits its verdict (7-day Pi logs on 2026-10-30: 110 of 119 calls). The reader counted only explicit verdicts, so session finding totals were mostly missing (blocking 18 vs 74 after the fix). **Fixed separately** in #329 by applying the observed Review receipt (ADR 0017).
- `SKILL.md` routes report reading but not follow-through. Questions about causes, friction or improvements have no route into the `dist/revisit.md` Follow-through method.
- The Report order puts usage, the tool histogram and `rounds/task` before any workflow answer. Follow-through step 8 requires a copy-ready TaskIntent or issue draft for every candidate (`dist/revisit.md`, locked by `tests/rework-root-cause-contract.test.ts`). That pushes toward volume rather than one supported next step.

## Proposed direction

Reposition `revisit` from a session statistics report to an evidence-based diagnosis of Immune-Brain workflow friction:

> Read-only inspection of one fixed window of real run evidence. Locate avoidable process friction, separate it from necessary user decisions and valid quality catches, and recommend at most one smallest improvement. When evidence is insufficient, say so.

One flow: **locate → verify → recommend.**

1. **Locate.** The analyzer lists a few *candidate* chains, never named as causes. Examples: the same task/run returning the same block repeatedly; a Reviewer with no valid verdict; a batch oscillating between incomplete and `needs_human`; a user input after which a stalled run resumed. Counts, short-message matches and repeated acceptance ids only help locate candidates.
2. **Verify.** For each selected candidate (default about 3), rebuild `prior state → actual stop/failure → user/Host action → next state` from evidence pointers. Classify it as necessary decision, valid quality catch, avoidable process friction, or unknown. The report states which candidates were checked and which were not.
3. **Recommend.** At most three findings, each written as `observation → causal evidence → counterexample or unknown → direction`. One recommended next step, or an explicit "not enough evidence to change anything".

Analysis target: the Immune-Brain workflow, not a business project's code quality. Evidence may come from any repository that uses Immune-Brain. Window and project scope are asked once and reused for follow-up questions.

## Candidate decisions (to settle in planning)

1. **Evidence output.** Add a machine-readable output to the existing reader (no second copy of sessions, no database or dashboard). It records the fixed window and scope; session, cwd, task_id and run_id (marked unknown when absent); timestamp, message id, line and `toolCallId`; call↔result links; and pointers back to the raw context. Every follow-up query in one analysis reuses this window.
2. **Sources keep their roles.** Sessions show human interaction, failures and recovery. Committed audit (`--audit`, ADR 0032) confirms terminal state, formal findings and assurance history. Neither is used to prove what only the other records.
3. **Report order.** The workflow answer leads. Usage, the tool histogram and `rounds/task` move to an appendix as locating context and are never used as a cause.
4. **Supersedes #322 / Spec `revisit-workflow-health` D6 in part.** Drop the per-candidate copy-ready TaskIntent or issue draft and give one recommendation by default, expanded on request. Full per-round tables and reading every finding apply only to the selected candidates, or when the user asks for a full retro.
5. **Regex labels become unverified markers.** Structured results take precedence, and what cannot be confirmed is `unknown` (affects `JITTER` and the bookkeeping regex naming).
6. **Routing.** `SKILL.md` adds a follow-through route ("cause / friction / how to improve") to the verify flow.

## Regression cases (counterexamples from the 2026-10-30 run)

1. 19 calls against one batch must not report "19 human confirmations".
2. `request_stop` → applied/stopped must not be listed as a lingering stall.
3. A long user message that carries a Skill plus a real instruction must not read as "no human input".
4. `submit_review` without a verdict but with an observed receipt must count its findings once (landed in #329).
5. An agent resuming after a quota error or tool interruption must not be judged a premature stop on "continue" alone.
6. A turn that ends with no block keeps enough context for a judgment. Whether a stop was unjustified stays semantic judgment, not regex.

Cases 1–4 are code-testable. Cases 5–6 need the evidence pointers plus agent judgment.

## Kept unchanged

Read-only. No Managed state resume or mutation. Audit reads committed HEAD only. Historical findings are not claimed as current bugs. Reduced friction never bypasses assurance.

## Suggested order

Evidence output and regression tests first, then slim the Skill and the contract. Rewording the contract alone leaves the next run with only a histogram, and the agent will scan logs ad hoc again.

## Out of scope

Snapshot/diff (#322 S4), Claude Code session reader, multi-agent orchestration, dashboards. Removing existing output fields only after their downstream consumers are checked (RVE-S1 reads `author` from the reader).

title: [revisit-evidence-chain] Evidence-chain diagnosis for revisit
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=revisit-evidence-chain -->

## Provenance

- Derived from #330: the originating feature Issue for this Initiative.

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

The revisit session reader skips every user and toolResult line, carries no line-level evidence pointers, derives its window from the current time so follow-up queries never share a window, and leads its report with usage and rounds/task statistics. The Skill routes only analyzer runs and report reading, and the contract asks for a copy-ready draft per candidate, so cause and friction questions get statistics instead of a diagnosis.

## Result

One flow, locate -> verify -> recommend: the analyzer emits a pointed evidence document over a fixed, reproducible window and lists candidate chains without causes; the contract verifies a few candidates against that evidence and recommends at most three findings with one next step or an explicit 'not enough evidence'.

## Initiative design

S1 owns the analyzer: the session reader moves to scripts/session_evidence.ts, review_retro.ts --json emits contract immune_brain/revisit_evidence/v1 (window, scope, pointed events, call-result links, candidate chains), --since/--until fix the window, the text report leads with candidate chains, and regex labels become unverified markers with unchanged totals. S2 owns the Skill and contract text: routing, locate -> verify -> recommend, source roles, report order, judgment rules, retirement of the per-candidate copy-ready draft, README and registry. S2 references only S1's public CLI and document, so S1 lands first and the two run serially (overlap on dist/revisit.md and the Spec). No Kernel, record, store or authority behavior changes; the committed-audit boundary of ADR 0032 is unchanged. Spec: docs/specs/revisit-evidence-chain.spec.md.

## Decisions

- Evidence output extends the existing reader; no session copy, database or analyzer-written file (#330 CD1).
- Sessions show interaction, failures and recovery; committed audit confirms terminal state, formal findings and assurance history (#330 CD2).
- The workflow answer leads; usage, tool histogram and rounds/task are an appendix never used as a cause (#330 CD3).
- The per-candidate copy-ready TaskIntent or issue draft from #322 is retired; a draft is written only on request (#330 CD4).
- Bookkeeping and jitter regex labels become unverified markers (#330 CD5).

## Testing strategy

S1 pins regression cases 1-3 and each candidate kind with a positive and a negative control in tests/review-retro-analyzer.test.ts and tests/review-retro-audit.test.ts; S2 asserts contract text, including absence of the retired copy-ready sentence, in tests/rework-root-cause-contract.test.ts and tests/skill-dist-consistency.test.ts. Agent judgment over evidence is a manual scenario.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-1` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: the agent runs revisit with --json and repeats it with the printed --since/--until. Then: it gets one document with an absolute window, scope, pointed events and call-result links, and the repeat reads exactly the same lines.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: they run revisit. Then: no tool call counts as human input, the Skill-wrapped message counts once, the applied stop is not a stall, and candidate chains carry pointers and no causes.
- `SCN-3` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: they ask where the workflow makes people step in and what to change first. Then: the Skill routes to the follow-through method rather than only report reading.
- `SCN-4` (Slice `S2`, manual): When: the agent follows locate -> verify -> recommend. Then: the write-up leads with at most three findings and one recommendation or 'not enough evidence', states which candidates were checked, and puts statistics in an appendix.

## Out of scope

- Snapshot/diff of reports (#322 S4).
- Claude Code session reader.
- Multi-agent orchestration and dashboards.
- Removing existing output fields before a consumer check; the author field stays for RVE-S1.

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: revisit --json yields a reproducible, pointed evidence document with candidate chains, and the text report leads with those chains.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: /revisit answers where the workflow makes people step in with at most three verified findings and one recommendation, or says the evidence is insufficient. (blocked by: revisit-evidence-chain-s1-evidence-output)

title: [Proposal] Revisit follow-up: group and triage candidate chains
body:
## Provenance

Follow-up to #330 (Initiative #332, PR #335: S1 `abbe38a`, S2 `431ad3e`). Settled in a design interview on 2026-11-01. #330 stays open until this lands and a manual SCN-4 run passes.

## Problem (verified)

On a real 7-day window (all projects, 2026-10-25T04:07Z to 2026-11-01T04:07Z), `review_retro.ts --json` emitted:

- **136 candidate chains**: 112 `user_resume` (37 distinct keys), 13 `repeated_block`, 11 `review_without_verdict`, 0 `batch_oscillation`. #330 asked for "a few candidates", and the contract verifies "about three", but nothing says how to pick three out of 136. The text report prints every occurrence with full session paths. Code: `plugins/immune-brain/skills/revisit/scripts/review_retro.ts:286-321` (one candidate per occurrence).
- **`user_resume` measures how often the user takes a turn, not friction.** A read-only sample of 10 candidates (one per distinct key, every 4th sorted key) gave: 2 avoidable friction, 4 necessary decisions, 3 error recovery, 1 unknown. Across all 112: 13 follow an `error`/`aborted` stop, and all 3 sampled ones were recovery. Narrowing by the blocking source of the stop does not work: sample #5 (a real acceptance-contract conflict) and #6 (friction) look the same at that point. The sample covers 10 of 112; the other 102 were not checked.
- **`sessions[]` lists 2262 files, but only 243 have events in the window** (`review_retro.ts:328-333` pushes every scanned session).

## Decisions

1. **Group candidates.** Group by `kind + key`. Each group carries `occurrences` and up to 5 pointers. The text report lists at most 5 groups per kind, ordered by occurrences (descending) then key, and prints `+N more groups (see --json)` for the rest. `--json` keeps every group as `{ kind, key, occurrences, pointers[] }`, and the contract becomes `immune_brain/revisit_evidence/v2`. No consumer reads `candidates` or `revisit_evidence/v1` outside the revisit scripts and tests (repository grep, 2026-11-01). Ordering by occurrences only helps locate candidates; it is not a severity, so D3's no-cause/no-severity rule holds.
2. **Split `error_resume` from `user_resume`.** A resume after an `error` or `aborted` stop becomes its own kind, `error_resume`. Each `user_resume` adds locating fields: a pointer to the last tool result before the stop, that result's `is_error`/`state`, and the character count of the user's reply. No content-based filter, no regex for short replies like "continue"/"继续" (#330 RC6, D5).
3. **`sessions[]` lists only sessions with in-window events.** Scope stays in `scope`.
4. **Selection rule in the contract** (`dist/revisit.md` Follow-through, Verify step): prefer the candidate groups that answer the user's question. With no clear pointer, take the group with the most occurrences of each kind, about three in total. List every group not selected as not checked. Kinds have no fixed priority over each other.
5. **Spec.** A new Spec (for example `revisit-candidate-triage`) supersedes `docs/specs/revisit-evidence-chain.spec.md` D1/D3/D4/D7 in part. The old Spec is not edited, because its intents are terminal. One Slice through the Managed path, with one `immune-brain` `minor` changeset.

## Testing

Positive and negative controls for grouping, truncation, the `error_resume` split, the `user_resume` locating fields and the `sessions[]` filter, in `tests/review-retro-analyzer.test.ts`. Contract text for the selection rule in `tests/rework-root-cause-contract.test.ts`.

## Acceptance after merge (manual SCN-4, closes #330)

In Pi, run `/revisit` on immune-brain over the 7 days before the merge and ask "where does the workflow make people step in, and what should change first?". The run passes only if:

1. It writes no ad-hoc JSONL scan beyond reading pointed lines.
2. Follow-up questions reuse the same `--since`/`--until`.
3. It states which candidates were checked and which were not.
4. It reports at most 3 findings, each `observation → evidence → counterexample/unknown → direction`.
5. It gives one recommendation, or says explicitly that there is not enough evidence.
6. Usage and `rounds/task` appear only in the appendix.
7. It violates none of #330 RC1–RC3.

The run's own session is then checked through `revisit --json`, with pointers.

## Out of scope

- Cross-kind priority or severity in the analyzer.
- Excluding candidates by the blocking source of the stop (counterexample: sample #5 vs #6).
- Snapshot/diff, the Claude Code session reader, dashboards (as in #330).

title: Cover the generated README role map in bun test so Managed QA catches registry drift
body:
## Problem

The plugin README role map is generated from the skill registry, but only CI checks it. No `bun test` file covers it, so a Managed run's QA (focused tests plus `bun run typecheck`) cannot catch the drift. The drift then shows up as a red CI check after the PR opens.

## Evidence

- `scripts/sync-dist-docs.ts:85-109` regenerates the block between `<!-- GENERATED: skill-registry-role-map -->` and its END marker in `plugins/immune-brain/README.md` from `plugins/immune-brain/skills/registry.yaml` (`scripts/skill-registry.ts:104` `renderReadmeRoleSection`, `:118` `REGISTRY_CANONICAL`).
- The only gate is `.github/workflows/ci.yml:48` (`bun scripts/sync-dist-docs.ts --check`) and the `verify:release` script (`package.json:33`).
- `grep -rln "skill-registry\|README_ROLE_MARKER\|renderReadmeRoleSection" tests/` returns nothing. `tests/dist-docs-sync-contract.test.ts` imports `scripts/dist-sync-manifest.ts` and guards mirror docs only.
- Observed case: `431ad3e` (#330 S2, Managed run) changed the `revisit` description in both registry copies and the root `README.md`, but not `plugins/immune-brain/README.md`. QA passed. The role map was fixed afterwards by hand in `072d5aa`, which touches only `plugins/immune-brain/README.md`.
- Found by the #330 SCN-3 walkthrough (Pi session `01a19636-4522-7338-bd8f-b5896cc5f35b`, finding F2).

## Proposed direction

Add a contract test that renders the role map from the canonical registry with `renderReadmeRoleSection(readSkillRegistry(root))` and asserts it equals the generated block in `plugins/immune-brain/README.md`. Add a negative control: a registry entry with a changed boundary yields a different block. Reuse the exported helpers; do not copy the rendering logic into the test.

Optional, only if it stays small: check `REGISTRY_COPIES` byte equality with `REGISTRY_CANONICAL` in the same test, since that is also CI-only today.

## Out of scope

- Changing `sync-dist-docs.ts` behavior or the README format.
- F1 from the same walkthrough (single-task enrollment and staged planning files). It relaxes the D23 invariant and needs its own design discussion first.

Refs #330.

title: [decision-models] Decision model integration
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=decision-models -->

## Provenance

- Derived from #204: the originating feature Issue for this Initiative.

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

Decision and classification calls across the workflow are made by ad hoc prompts or not at all, and #204's convergence trigger has no deterministic count to fire on.

## Result

A shared decision-model component with configurable Jev and Clef providers, a shared offline eval harness, the per-acceptance repeat series and convergence trigger, and offline evals for A4, A15 and A16.

## Initiative design

Phase 0 (decision-model-core, PR #341) shipped the component under scripts/, outside runtime/ (ADR 0006). One provider per decision, configured per point; a failed or unavailable provider falls back to today's deterministic behavior. Sensitive input categories leave the machine only when the tracked bindings egress list enables them. S1 builds the per-acceptance repeat series once from committed records; S2 consumes it in the review rework handoff, and S5 reports against it. S4 is the shared eval harness that S5, S6 and S7 build on. S5, S6 and S7 each register a point in scripts/decision-model/thresholds.ts and run one at a time; S3 shares files with S4 and S7 and runs before them. Live use of any point needs its own offline report first and is added by amendment.

## Decisions

- Models only advise or tighten in Managed, Review and Kernel layers; standalone skills may act on above-threshold results except security and red-circle findings (BR-DEC-1).
- One provider per decision; no ensembles or fallback chains (BR-DEC-2).
- Only decision models with native per-option probabilities, plus a fake provider for tests (BR-DEC-5).
- S2 adds the obligation to the rework handoff only; Kernel parking is unchanged.
- issue_text is non-sensitive because the repository is public.

## Testing strategy

Every slice is verified offline with the fake provider or a replaced fetch; no network or credentials in tests. Real-provider eval runs need user-supplied credentials and labelled corpora and are not part of acceptance.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-1` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: they run the acceptance repeat report. Then: they see, per run and acceptance, the finding count, rounds since the last finding and the current streak.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: Review returns rework on the same acceptance again. Then: the rework handoff names the generalize-or-refute obligation for that acceptance.
- `SCN-3` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: Review returns rework. Then: the rework handoff is the same as today.
- `SCN-4` (Slice `S3`, automated): When: they run the A14 offline eval. Then: the report shows Jev as the provider.
- `SCN-5` (Slice `S4`, automated): When: they run the A14 offline eval. Then: the report keeps its existing numbers and adds a calibration section.
- `SCN-6` (Slice `S5`, automated): When: they run the A4 offline eval. Then: every case shows unavailable because the category is not enabled, and no request is sent.
- `SCN-7` (Slice `S6`, automated): When: they run the A16 offline eval. Then: they see the classification report next to the baseline.
- `SCN-8` (Slice `S7`, automated): When: they run the A15 offline eval. Then: they see the triage report next to the baseline.

## Out of scope

- A14 live use in fix-pr and A4 live Advisory (#204 S3): need their offline reports first
- A13 scope drift scoring: only 3 committed records carry beyond_estimate
- A8 and A11: no committed batch records to label from
- A10 and A12: label sources unverified
- A6 and A7: Phase 3, after Phase 1 evidence
- A1-A3 migration, A5 sampling, A9 risk suggestion, A17 drift classes (needs a #316 revision), rework budget unit: deferred during clarification

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: Per-acceptance review repeat counts computed from committed records, with a read-only report.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: The rework handoff names a design-level obligation when the same acceptance repeats in consecutive review rounds. (blocked by: acceptance-repeat-series)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S3 --> **S3**: Jev (TypeSafe System One) is a configurable decision-model provider for choice questions.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S4 --> **S4**: One shared offline eval harness for corpus, metrics, calibration and baseline comparison.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S5 --> **S5**: Offline eval of whether a decision model groups repeated findings by invariant class. (blocked by: acceptance-repeat-series, decision-eval-harness)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S6 --> **S6**: Offline eval of revisit candidate chain classification. (blocked by: decision-eval-harness)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S7 --> **S7**: Offline eval of issue triage against the repository's own labels. (blocked by: decision-eval-harness)
