title: Batch integration parks clean merges of a file changed by two children
body:
## Problem

A batch child is parked as `batch_integration_conflict` when it and an already-integrated sibling both changed the same file in non-conflicting places, even though `git merge-tree` merges the two cleanly.

Observed in Initiative `decision-models` (#349):
- S3 `jev-adapter` and S4 `decision-eval-harness` ran in parallel. Both changed `tests/decision-eval-a14.test.ts`: S4 added one assertion near line 121, and S3 added one test after line 135.
- S3 was integrated first (`c15085b`).
- S4's integration was refused with: `batch_integration_conflict: candidate 8ce0f9dcce9f4bac5abc4708f1563a0cae6a5466 does not carry the lane commit 90726e6ce33454ec83f627cc77397ec3f9f3a1c0 change`. The child parked as `batch_lane_redo_retained`, and its dependents S5, S6 and S7 were skipped.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=c3363a8 <batch head> 90726e6` exits 0, so the merge has no conflicts. The candidate `8ce0f9d` carries every path of S4's change. Only the blob of the shared test file differs from the lane commit, and it should, because that file also holds S3's change.

## Cause

`laneCandidateMatches` in `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/unattended/batch_integration.ts:179` rejects every clean merge that touches a file a sibling also changed:

1. **Exact per-path identity.** The fast path compares `changeIdentity(lane_base, lane_commit)` with `changeIdentity(batch_head, candidate)` blob by blob. This always fails when the sibling changed the same path.
2. **Conflict-only fallback.** The fallback reruns `merge-tree` and accepts only when it returns `1`, meaning conflicts resolved by derived-file regeneration. A clean merge returns `0`, so the check hits `if (merged.status !== 1) return false;`.

The scheduler was changed in `60d1541` (ADR 0028 item 2, `docs/adr/0028-scope-as-estimate.md:28`: "Overlapping estimates run concurrently; the merge queue resolves real conflicts") to run overlapping scopes together. The integration check was not relaxed to match, so any overlap on a shared file now parks the later child, even when there is no real conflict.

## Expected

A clean tree-level merge of the lane change onto the batch head is accepted when the candidate's tree equals the rebuilt merge tree. A real content conflict that derived-file regeneration does not resolve is still refused.

## Acceptance

- Two Lanes change different hunks of the same file. The second one integrates as one commit whose tree carries both changes.
- A tampered candidate is still refused, i.e. one whose tree differs from the rebuilt merge tree. The existing check in `tests/derived-files.test.ts:91` keeps passing.
- A real content conflict in a non-derived file is still refused as `batch_integration_conflict` and does not move the batch ref.
- Recovery (`findIntegratedCandidate`, `batch_git.ts:736`, `batch_git.ts:922`) accepts the same clean-merge candidates, so a restart does not re-park an integrated child.

## Related stale docs

`plugins/immune-brain/dist/drive-batch.md:178` still says "Only children whose scopes are provably disjoint run together". This contradicts ADR 0028 item 2 and current scheduling.

title: Batch parks a Lane whose change a sibling already delivered identically
body:
## Problem

A Lane whose change an integrated sibling already delivered identically is parked as `batch_integration_conflict`, even though nothing conflicts.

`laneCandidateMatches` (`plugins/immune-brain/runtime/unattended/batch_integration.ts:186-197`) refuses whenever the rebuilt merge tree equals the batch head tree (`:194`). The #357 fix added this guard to keep `tests/unattended-batch-lanes.test.ts` "refuses a candidate whose change differs from the lane commit and leaves the batch branch unmoved" passing. Without it, a clean merge would produce an empty integration commit.

`plugins/immune-brain/dist/drive-batch.md` now states that the merge queue "refuses only a real conflict" (ADR 0028 item 2). A duplicate delivery is not a real conflict, so the documented rule and the runtime disagree for this case.

Source: advisory finding `review-1` from the independent Review of task `batch-clean-overlap-integration` (operation `21158fe1-e0ea-4fce-8263-bbb8ae6532c6`). No test pins the current behaviour.

## Trigger

Sibling and Lane make the same edit to one file. `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 and the rebuilt tree equals the batch head tree. `laneCandidateMatches` returns false and `prepareLaneCandidate` throws `batch_integration_conflict`.

## Options (not decided)

1. Settle the child as integrated with no new commit when its change is already on the batch head, and record the existing head as its integration evidence. Restart adoption (`findIntegratedCandidate`) must still refuse a tampered head.
2. Keep refusing, but use a distinct reason (for example `batch_change_already_present`), state it in `drive-batch.md`, and add a test.

Either option needs a test for the duplicate-delivery case. It must keep the existing tamper refusals: extra hunk, extra path, and a change that differs from the lane commit.

title: Layered user/project configuration for Immune-Brain (plugin-level, Claude Code + Pi)
body:
## Problem

Immune-Brain configuration is scattered across per-clone local files, tracked JSON and parsed instruction-file prose, and none of it is plugin-level:

| Setting | Today | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| Lane presets (`max_parallel`, Executor host/model/effort) | `.imm/lanes.local.json`, gitignored, read by the Parent Skill only (ADR 0033) | Personal setting stored per clone; every clone and machine needs its own copy |
| Decision-model profiles (provider, model, credential env var names) | `.imm/decision-models.local.json`, gitignored (`scripts/decision-model/config.ts:27`) | Same; absent inside Lane worktrees, so a Lane Executor would get `no_local_config` |
| Decision-point bindings + `egress` | `.imm/decision-bindings.json`, tracked (`config.ts:26`) | Mixes personal profile names with project data-governance policy |
| Git integration | `- Git integration:` line parsed from tracked `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` (`runtime/git_integration_preference.ts:20`, ADR 0024) | Runtime parses prose |
| Initiative carrier default | Instruction-file directive read by the Skill LLM | Not machine-readable; no source reporting |

The decision-model component itself lives in repository `scripts/decision-model/`, and `docs/specs/decision-model-core.spec.md` forbids the plugin runtime from importing it, so no other project that installs the plugin can use it.

Observed: the two retained `revisit-evidence-chain` Lane worktrees have `.imm/audit`, `.imm/state` and `.imm/risk-floor.json` but neither `*.local.json` file.

## Confirmed decisions (repository owner, 2026-11-02)

1. **User-level file**: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/immune-brain/config.json` (default `~/.config/immune-brain/config.json`), one file shared by Claude Code and Pi. Not Claude `userConfig`/`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` (Claude-only, flat scalars, unreadable by Pi), not `~/.pi/agent/` (Pi-only).
2. **Move the decision-model component into the plugin runtime** (`plugins/immune-brain/runtime/`), shipped in the Claude bundle and the Pi extension. Offline eval scripts may stay in `scripts/` and import from the runtime.
3. **Project-level file**: tracked `.imm/config.json`. Git integration and Initiative carrier move into the layered config too, and Lane configuration moves into it as well.

## Proposed design (to be settled in draw-up)

- **User level** holds personal settings: decision-model profiles, Lane profiles, the active profile names, decision-point to profile bindings, personal Initiative carrier default. Per-project overrides keyed by normalized `origin` URL (`projects["github.com/owner/repo"]`), so every clone, worktree and Lane of one repository reads the same values. Credentials stay env var names only.
- **Project level** (`.imm/config.json`) holds repository facts and policy: enabled decision points, `egress` ceiling for sensitive input categories, `git_integration`, Initiative carrier, Lane defaults/limits, batch final verification commands. `.imm/risk-floor.json` stays a separate file (ADR 0023 fail-to-critical rule).
- **Resolution**: personal keys resolve request > user project-override > user global > project default > built-in. Policy keys (`egress`, enabled decision points, `git_integration`) are owned by the project; the user level may only tighten `egress`, never widen it.
- **Readers**: one runtime resolver used by Claude MCP server and Pi extension; Lane Executors resolve the same values because the user file and the tracked project file are both reachable from a Lane worktree.
- **Observability**: the `status` Tool reports each effective value with its source (`request` / `project` / `user` / `default`) and any diagnostics; malformed config fails closed with a named diagnostic.
- **Migration**: legacy sources (`.imm/lanes.local.json`, `.imm/decision-models.local.json`, `.imm/decision-bindings.json`, the instruction-file `Git integration` and `Initiative carrier default` directives) are read for one major version with a deprecation warning naming the replacement key, then removed. Changeset is a major.

## Decisions superseded

- `docs/reference/immune-brain-config.md` principle "Immune-Brain loads no agent-local file".
- ADR 0024 item 1 (instruction-file directive as the Git integration source).
- ADR 0033 (Lane preferences in a per-clone local preset read only by the Parent).
- `docs/specs/decision-model-core.spec.md` D3 (two config files) and the runtime import ban.

A new ADR records the layered config and supersedes the above.

## Open questions for draw-up

- Key for per-project user overrides when a repository has no `origin` remote (fallback to the absolute main-checkout path?).
- Whether Lane defaults at project level are defaults or hard caps (e.g. `max_parallel` ceiling).
- Whether the Initiative carrier remains Skill-read (via `status` output) or becomes runtime-enforced.

## Related

- #204 decision-model integration (configuration is a prerequisite for real offline evals and rollout).
- #349 decision-models Initiative (delivered component being moved).

title: [layered-config] Layered configuration
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=layered-config -->

## Provenance

- Derived from #360: the originating feature Issue for this Initiative.

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

Personal settings live in per-clone gitignored files that Lane worktrees and other clones never see, policy and personal values share one tracked file, Git integration and the carrier are parsed from instruction prose, and the decision-model component lives outside the plugin.

## Result

One user file at ~/.config/immune-brain/config.json with per-repository overrides, one tracked .imm/config.json for project policy and defaults, one resolver used by both Hosts and every Lane, and the decision-model component shipped with the plugin.

## Initiative design

S1 moves the decision-model component unchanged into plugins/immune-brain/runtime/decision_model/; authority paths still never import it. S2 adds resolveConfig(root) with imm-kernel config --json and a status config field; it has no consumer until S3-S5. Personal values resolve request > user per-repository override > user global > project default > built-in; policy values (enabled points, egress ceiling, git_integration) come from the project, and the user may only narrow egress. Per-repository overrides are keyed by the normalized origin URL, else the main checkout path, so every clone, worktree and Lane resolves alike. S3, S4 and S5 each switch one consumer and keep the legacy source with a deprecation warning; they run in parallel and share only the Spec and the generated Claude bundle. S6 documents the result last. risk-floor.json stays a separate file.

## Decisions

- User file is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/immune-brain/config.json, shared by Claude Code and Pi (#360 decision 1).
- The decision-model component moves into the plugin runtime (#360 decision 2).
- Git integration, Initiative carrier and Lane settings move into the layered config (#360 decision 3).
- Credentials stay env var names only; values are never stored or echoed.
- Legacy sources are read for one major version with a warning; removal is deferred.
- ADR 0034 supersedes ADR 0033, ADR 0024 item 1 and decision-model-core D3.

## Testing strategy

Every slice is verified with temporary repositories and an isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME; tests never read the real user config, network or credentials. Mirror, bundle and typecheck checks guard the generated outputs.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-5` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: they run imm-kernel config --json. Then: each value still applies with a legacy source and a deprecation warning names the replacement key.
- `SCN-6` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: they run imm-kernel config --json. Then: the CLI names the file and key path, never echoes the value, and exits 1.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S3`, automated): When: they run the A14 offline eval from a Lane worktree. Then: the eval calls the bound provider instead of reporting no local config.
- `SCN-4` (Slice `S3`, automated): When: they run an A4 eval with a clef profile. Then: every A4 case is unavailable with egress denied.
- `SCN-3` (Slice `S4`, automated): When: they read status for a task. Then: git_integration shows auto with source .imm/config.json.
- `SCN-1` (Slice `S5`, manual): When: they start a batch from either clone. Then: the Parent's preference line shows the profile's values with source user in both clones.

## Out of scope

- Enabling a live decision point: A14 and A4 rollout stays with #204
- Removing legacy config sources: a later major version
- Merging risk-floor.json into the project file
- Claude userConfig or keychain integration

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: The decision-model component ships with the plugin under plugins/immune-brain/runtime/decision_model/, unchanged in behaviour; offline eval scripts import it from there.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: One runtime resolver reads ~/.config/immune-brain/config.json and the tracked .imm/config.json, with per-repository overrides, legacy fallbacks, diagnostics, imm-kernel config --json and a status config field on both Hosts. (blocked by: config-decision-model-move)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S3 --> **S3**: Decision-model profiles and bindings come from the user file and enabled points and the egress ceiling from the project file, so evals work from any clone or Lane. (blocked by: config-decision-model-move, config-resolver)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S4 --> **S4**: Git integration and the Initiative carrier are read from .imm/config.json through the resolver, with the instruction-file directives kept as deprecated fallbacks. (blocked by: config-resolver)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S5 --> **S5**: The Parent resolves Lane parallelism, Executor Host, model and effort through the layered config and shows each value's source. (blocked by: config-resolver)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S6 --> **S6**: The config reference, both READMEs and IMMUNE.md describe the layered model. (blocked by: config-decision-model-consumer, config-git-carrier, config-lanes)

title: deprecated_config_source warning omits the replacement key's layer
body:
## Problem

Spec `docs/specs/layered-config.spec.md` D9 says a legacy value "adds a `deprecated_config_source` warning naming the replacement key", and the D9 table names each replacement with its layer (user `lanes`, project `git_integration`, user `decision_models` / project `decision_models.egress`, ...).

The warning built in `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/config/layered_config.ts:121-124` (the `legacy` helper) puts only the bare key in `key_path` and a fixed sentence in `message`:

```
.imm/lanes.local.json: lanes: deprecated; use this replacement key
```

Observed in `status` on `imm/layered-config` (`fcffb25`) with a maintainer `.imm/lanes.local.json` present.

Two gaps:

1. The message does not say which file the replacement key belongs in (user `~/.config/immune-brain/config.json` vs project `.imm/config.json`). For `lanes` the right target is the user file; nothing in the warning says so.
2. `.imm/decision-bindings.json` has a split replacement (personal `default_profile`/`bindings` → user `decision_models`, `egress` ceiling → project `decision_models.egress`), but the call at `layered_config.ts:137` passes only `decision_models`, so the egress half of the migration is not named at all.

`legacy_source_ignored` (same helper) has the same wording gap.

## Expected

Each `deprecated_config_source` / `legacy_source_ignored` message names the replacement key together with its layer, matching the D9 table, e.g. `deprecated; move to user lanes in ~/.config/immune-brain/config.json`, and the decision-bindings case names both targets.

## Notes

- Severity: low. Resolution and precedence are unaffected; only the migration hint is incomplete.
- Found while finishing #361 (PR #368).

title: Planner ignores the legacy repository carrier directive that D9 says is still read
body:
## Problem

The layered-config Spec says the legacy `- Initiative carrier default:` line in a tracked `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` is still read for one major version, with a deprecation warning. The Planner contract tells draw-up to ignore that value. The runtime and the Planner therefore disagree on the carrier in one case.

## Evidence

- **Spec says read it:** `docs/specs/layered-config.spec.md:181` (D9) maps `- Initiative carrier default:` in tracked `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` to `initiative_carrier`, read for one major version with `deprecated_config_source`.
- **Runtime reads it:**
  - `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/config/layered_config.ts:180` reads the directive from tracked `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`.
  - `tests/layered-config.test.ts:136` asserts `initiative_carrier.source` is `legacy:AGENTS.md`.
- **Planner contract says ignore it:**
  - `plugins/immune-brain/dist/draw-up.md:229-231`, step 2: "use `initiative_carrier.value` … ignore a `legacy:AGENTS.md` or `legacy:CLAUDE.md` repository directive".
  - The user guide repeats this at `docs/reference/immune-brain-config.md:142-143`.
- This came in with S4 (`config-git-carrier`, integrated in `bfc2338`, merged in #368).

## Failure scenario

A repository has no `.imm/config.json` `initiative_carrier`, but its tracked `AGENTS.md` still has `- Initiative carrier default: github`. Then:

1. `imm-kernel config --json` reports `initiative_carrier: github`, with source `legacy:AGENTS.md` and a deprecation warning.
2. draw-up skips that value and falls through to the user-level instruction-file directive, or asks.

The user sees a resolved value in `config` that the Planner does not use. This repository is not affected, because `.imm/config.json` sets `initiative_carrier`.

## Proposed fix

Align draw-up with D9.

- In step 2, accept a `legacy:<path>` value like any other source, report the source, and pass the deprecation warning on to the user.
- Update `docs/reference/immune-brain-config.md` to match.
- Removal stays deferred to the next major release, as D9 says.

Not verified: whether the same "ignore legacy" wording exists for `git_integration` anywhere outside the runtime. The runtime path at `layered_config.ts:180` covers both keys.

title: Merge queue accepts a Lane that leaves a declared derived output stale on a clean merge
body:
## Problem

A Lane can change a declared derived-file source without regenerating its output, and the merge queue accepts it. The stale output then sits on the batch head. Every later sibling fails `build-claude-plugin.ts --check` in its integration check, and the failure is reported against the sibling instead of the Lane that caused it.

#277 (branch-boundary-r2 S3) regenerates derived outputs only when `merge-tree` reports a conflict on a declared output. A clean merge that leaves an output stale is not covered.

## Evidence

- `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/unattended/batch_integration.ts:128-139`: `buildCandidate` runs the declared `generate`/`check` only inside `if (merged.status === 1)`, for entries whose outputs are among the conflicted paths. A clean merge (exit 0) runs neither.
- `docs/agents/derived-files.json` declares `claude-mcp-bundle`:
  - its sources include `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/**/*.ts`;
  - its output is `plugins/immune-brain/dist/claude/mcp-server.mjs`.
- Batch `batch-layered-config-d295124a-dd3f-4beb-8705-c28db7188284`, S5 `config-lanes`:
  - Lane commit `5829cff` changes `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/config/layered_config.ts` but not `mcp-server.mjs` (same 1041850-byte blob before and after).
  - It was batch-integrated.
- S3 `config-decision-model-consumer` and S4 `config-git-carrier` then parked as `batch_integration_conflict`. Their integration checks failed `build-claude-plugin.ts --check` on the stale bundle; see the `bfc2338` commit message. They were integrated by hand in `bfc2338`, with the bundle regenerated once from the combined tree.
- #277 AC4 makes final verification run every declared check. That catches the drift only at the end, after siblings have already parked.

## Failure scenario

1. Lane A changes a file under `runtime/**/*.ts` and does not regenerate the bundle. Its own verification does not run `--check`.
2. Lane A integrates on a clean merge, and the batch head now carries a stale bundle.
3. Lane B integrates next. Its integration check runs `--check` on a candidate built on that head, fails, and B is parked as `batch_lane_redo_retained`. Per ADR 0028, B is not redone in this batch.
4. Every later Lane parks the same way, until the batch is integrated by hand.

## Proposed fix

When a Lane's delta touches a declared source, treat the clean-merge candidate like the conflict case:

- run the entry's `generate` then `check` in the delivery workspace;
- accept the result only if it changes nothing beyond the declared outputs, which is the same guard as the conflict path.

If `generate` or `check` fails, park that Lane with a reason that names the derived entry. It is the Lane that introduced the drift, not a later sibling.

Not verified: whether Lane QA or Review could also require `--check` when a declared source changes. That would catch the drift earlier, but on its own it does not protect the queue.

title: [merge-queue-followups] Merge queue follow-ups
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=merge-queue-followups -->

## Provenance

- Derived from #371: the originating feature Issue for this Initiative.

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites this Parent after creation; the tracker closes it as completed once every Slice Child is completed, and never closes it otherwise.

## Problem

The merge queue regenerates derived outputs such as dist/claude/mcp-server.mjs only when a merge conflicts on a declared output. A clean merge can therefore leave the bundle stale, and a later sibling parks for it (#371). A Lane whose whole change is already on the batch head is refused as batch_integration_conflict, although nothing conflicts (#359).

## Result

A Lane that touches a declared source or output integrates with that output regenerated from the merged tree, and a failed regeneration parks that Lane. A fully duplicated delivery parks with batch_change_already_present, while a Lane sharing one identical edit with a sibling still integrates.

## Initiative design

S1 changes buildCandidate in batch_integration.ts to select declared derived entries by the Lane's changed paths and to run generate then check in the merged tree on clean merges, declared-output conflicts and the no-conflict fast path; regeneration may change only declared outputs, and laneCandidateMatches still proves a candidate by rebuilding it. S2 adds the BatchIntegrationReason batch_change_already_present for a rebuilt tree equal to the batch head and parks it with that reason in batch_lanes.ts instead of batch_lane_redo_retained. S2 follows S1 because both edit buildCandidate and laneCandidateMatches and both regenerate the Claude bundle. drive-batch.md states both behaviours. No persisted record shape, authority gate or cross-Host contract changes.

## Decisions

- Regenerate on a clean merge as well as on a declared-output conflict, selecting entries by the Lane's changed paths (#371).
- Keep refusing a fully duplicated delivery, with its own reason, documented and tested (#359 option 2, user decision 2026-11-02).

## Testing strategy

Temporary Git repositories with a fake derived declaration exercise clean, conflicting and fast-path merges, including failing and path-escaping generators; one two-child Parent batch test covers the end-to-end case; a contract text test pins drive-batch.md.

## User scenarios

- `SCN-1` (Slice `S1`, automated): When: the merge queue integrates both. Then: both children integrate with no park, and the bundle on the Parent branch passes its declared --check.
- `SCN-2` (Slice `S2`, automated): When: the merge queue tries to integrate it. Then: the child parks with batch_change_already_present and the batch head does not move.

## Out of scope

- Lane-side --check enforcement in QA or Review
- Settling a fully duplicated child as integrated (#359 option 1)
- #369 and #370

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: A Lane that leaves a declared derived output stale integrates with it regenerated from the merged tree, and later siblings no longer park on it.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: A fully duplicated Lane delivery parks with batch_change_already_present, and a partially duplicated one integrates as before. (blocked by: derived-regenerate-on-change)

title: Planner resolves a legacy carrier but does not report its source or deprecation warning
body:
## Problem

When `initiative_carrier` resolves from a `legacy:AGENTS.md` repository directive, draw-up uses the value but never shows the user where it came from or that the source is deprecated. The user gets no prompt to move the setting to `.imm/config.json`.

This is the manual scenario SCN-2 of `docs/specs/legacy-config-hints.spec.md`, left unverified in #376. #370 fixed the contract text (step 2 no longer ignores `legacy:<path>`); this issue is about the Planner not following that text.

## Evidence

Manual run on 2026-11-03, plugin loaded from repository source (`--plugin-dir plugins/immune-brain`, skill Base directory confirmed under the repo, not the 7.0.0 cache). Test repo: one committed `AGENTS.md` containing `- Initiative carrier default: github`; no `.imm/config.json`; no `initiative_carrier` in the user config.

- Session `5b85a62b-0355-48a7-9a47-f4669a263bb9`, lines 109–110: `imm-kernel config --json` returned `initiative_carrier = {value: github, source: legacy:AGENTS.md}` and the warning `deprecated; move to project \`initiative_carrier\` in .imm/config.json`.
- Lines 116–118: the Planner went straight to an `AskUserQuestion` about decomposition and Initiative destination. It treated the carrier as GitHub (thinking: "The GitHub carrier can't publish yet because this repo has no Git remote") but printed no visible text.
- After line 110 the transcript contains `legacy:AGENTS.md` 0 times and `deprecated` 0 times.

Contract requirements that were skipped:

- `plugins/immune-brain/dist/draw-up.md:231-232`: "for a `legacy:<path>` source also report its `deprecated_config_source` warning, which names the replacement".
- `plugins/immune-brain/dist/draw-up.md:242`: "display one non-blocking line with the selected carrier and its source".

Runtime output (AC1/AC2) and contract text (AC3) of #376 are correct. Whether this omission is occasional or consistent: not verified (one sample).

## Expected

Before any question about decomposition or carrier destination, draw-up displays one line naming the selected carrier and its source, and for a `legacy:<path>` source the deprecation warning naming the replacement layer, key, and file.

## Suggested direction

- Move the display requirement from the end of the paragraph at line 242 into step 2 as a required output, stating that the source line and any `deprecated_config_source` warning appear before any `AskUserQuestion`.
- Pin the ordering with a contract test beside the existing `legacy:<path>` assertions in `tests/carrier-enrollment-gate-contract.test.ts` and `tests/pi-only-current-contracts.test.ts`.
- Re-run SCN-2 at least twice after the change.

title: Pi 扩展缺少用户可达的 stop 入口，workspace claim 死锁（复现与源码证据）
body:
# Pi 扩展缺少用户可达的 stop 入口，workspace claim 死锁（复现与源码证据）

## 问题

Immune-Brain Kernel 运行时支持 `stop` 终态操作（含专用理由 "literal user stopped task parked for replan"），但 Pi 扩展（`.pi-extension/`）没有把任何用户可达入口接到它上面。结果是：一旦一个 active 任务因「scope 外缺陷需转独立任务」而必须让出 workspace claim，agent 与用户都无路可走，后续任务全部被 `kernel_owner_active` 拒绝，形成死锁。

## 复现（本项目实际发生，2026-09-07）

1. 任务 `issue-16b-founder-comprehension-gate`（TaskRecord v4，`active:active`，risk material）持有唯一 workspace claim（`.imm/state/workspace.json` 的 `current_working`）。
2. 真机重新冻结阶段发现一个集成缺陷：`WelltoldUITests/SleepCurrentStatusJourneyTests.swift:99` 的断言落在 retention-e0 改动前的旧深链目标上（真机 15.3s / 模拟器三次一致失败，隔离探针证明深链行为正常、断言过期）。修复需要编辑 `WelltoldUITests/`，该路径不在 16B 的 `scope_hint` 内；且 intent goal 明文「本任务不获得任何 integration 修复授权」。Spec PD-03 已按流程 fail-closed 转独立任务。
3. 尝试为独立修复任务 author 新 TaskIntent：`imm-kernel intent author` → `kernel_owner_active: an active Kernel claim already owns this workspace; authoring is blocked`。
4. 尝试一切 agent 侧合法手段释放 claim，全部被拒：
   - `approve_breaking_intent_revision`（把修复塑进 16B）→ `intent revision cannot change goal or owner`（goal 不可变，而 goal 原文禁止修复）；
   - `request_authorization` → `no unique host-derived authorization operation`（投影无 open user decision，不弹授权对话框）；
   - 工具面没有 stop op。

## 源码证据（plugin 3.6.1）

| 事实 | 位置 |
| --- | --- |
| Kernel 支持 stop 且要求 user authority capability：`stop requires user authority capability` | `runtime/kernel/canary_application.ts:324` |
| stop 专用理由已在扩展内实现："literal user stopped task parked for replan" | `.pi-extension/imm-canary-work.ts:946-947` |
| `authorizeExactOperation` 的全部调用点只有 2 处（breaking-revision 与 `request_authorization` 派生），没有任何调用点传 `"stop"` | `.pi-extension/imm-canary-work.ts:545, 1035`（定义 704） |
| `request_authorization` 只派生 `resolve-user-decision` / `authorize-rework`，永不派生 stop | `.pi-extension/imm-canary-work.ts:1047-1056` |
| `imm_kernel_canary` 工具 schema 恰好 10 个 op，无 stop | `.pi-extension/imm-canary-work.ts:425-455` |
| `/imm-tasks` overlay 只读（`presentTaskOverviewOverlay` 只处理 esc/q 关闭） | `.pi-extension/pi-canary-interaction.ts:253-287` |
| `imm-canary-enroll.ts` 只注册 `imm_canary_enrollment`（action: "new"） | `.pi-extension/imm-canary-enroll.ts:570-600` |
| enrollment 在 claim 冲突时的提示本身就指向缺口：`Workspace is owned by …; finish or stop the current owner first` —— 但 stop 入口不存在 | `.pi-extension/imm-canary-enroll.ts:435` |

USER_GUIDE.md:81 也写明「显式 stop … 使用各自的单次 current-Host native authority gate」，但该 gate 在 Pi 扩展中没有用户可达入口。

## 影响

- 任何「fail-closed 转独立任务」的正规路径（这正是 workflow 的设计语义）在 Pi 宿主上都会死锁：旧任务无法终止、新任务无法登记，连 planning（intent author）都被拒。
- agent 无权自救（stop 要求 literal-user capability 是正确的），但用户同样没有按钮 —— 特权操作缺少宿主接线，而不是缺少权限。

## 建议修法（任选其一或并用）

1. **`/imm-tasks` overlay 增加操作项**：对 active 任务提供 Stop（以及必要的授权确认框），复用 `authorizeExactOperation(taskId, "stop", ctx)` 与现成的 reason 文案。
2. **扩展 `imm_kernel_canary` schema 增加 `op: "stop"`**（privileged、TUI-only，弹 `requestAuthorityDialog`），使 agent 可以在 Kernel 校验的 literal-user capability 前提下请求用户确认 —— 对话框本身就是 literal-user 授权面。
3. 文档同步：USER_GUIDE 写明 stop 的宿主入口（当前只有 Claude MCP server 有 `{ name: "stop", …, privileged: true }`，Pi 侧缺失，见 `runtime/claude/mcp_server.ts:27`）。

## 环境

- plugin version: 3.6.1（`imm-kernel status --json` → `plugin_version`）
- Host: Pi（TUI 模式）
- 复现仓库：Welltold（local carrier initiative，TaskRecord v4）

## 附：死锁期间的现场快照

- `.imm/state/workspace.json`: `current_working = issue-16b-founder-comprehension-gate`
- TaskRecord: `lifecycle=active, artifact_state=active`，1 blocking finding（`journey-expectation-stale-after-retention-e0`），0 open user decisions
- 16B Spec PD-03（`docs/specs/issue-16b-founder-comprehension-gate.spec.md`，commit 7070e52）已记录完整根因链与两次被拒的 revision 尝试

title: Improve Review convergence with verified finding history and snapshot-bound coverage
body:
## Problem

The S3 batch state-machine task (#45, delivery commit 6548e30) required repeated full-diff reviews. Some rounds found genuine recovery and authorization defects; others repeated findings contradicted by the enclosing call chain and executable tests. Changing the reviewer model alone did not eliminate this pattern.

Examples from the completed work:
- An alleged symlink write bypass ignored the outer Kernel store lock. Regression tests verified rejection for .imm, .imm/state, and the batch directory with no external writes.
- A dependent-reset allegation was contradicted by the successful recovery path and a direct regression test.
- Real defects included inconsistent child selection during recovery and renewed capabilities losing consumed-child history. A recovery matrix and tests using real deriveChildEnrollment exposed these gaps more effectively than repeated isolated patches.
- Editing a frozen snapshot before submitting a verdict invalidated review evidence and forced repeated assurance.

## Desired Outcome

Reduce repeated discovery cost without weakening independent Review, frozen-snapshot freshness, or critical-task security checks. This is a separate framework improvement, not a blocker for S4 (#46).

## Recommended Investigation

1. Preserve a bounded history of findings, their dispositions, and executable counterevidence. A claimed fix or rejection is not itself proof.
2. Distinguish initial full review from repair verification. Study whether unchanged coverage can be reused with exact snapshot and dependency bindings; require a full review when coverage becomes invalid or uncertain.
3. Require actionable findings to identify trigger conditions, the relevant caller chain, and the violated acceptance or concrete security boundary. Do not turn speculative threat-model expansion into automatic blocking work.
4. After two rounds that continue to add independent defects, pause the patch/review cycle for a concentrated boundary test matrix and disputed-finding verification. This is a diagnostic trigger, never an automatic pass or a limit on valid findings.
5. Measure elapsed time, tokens, repeated/refuted findings, newly verified defects, and rework rounds before and after changes. Scope evidence collection to this project's sessions and framework code.

## Acceptance Candidates

- A previously refuted finding is not treated as new merely because the next reviewer lacks its evidence; stale counterevidence is explicitly invalidated.
- A real defect introduced by a repair remains discoverable, including changes that affect an unchanged caller.
- Old snapshot verdicts cannot be submitted as current approval.
- Missing or invalid review evidence remains fail-closed; no limit on review rounds can authorize completion.
- Reviewer coverage reuse, if adopted, has deterministic invalidation tests and does not create a second workflow authority.

## Non-goals

Kernel core redesign, generic scheduling frameworks, parallel Managed tasks, model-only fixes, automatic acceptance of reviewer claims, and lowering risk-tier assurance requirements.

## Status

Recorded for follow-up at user request. No Spec, TaskIntent, Enrollment, or implementation is authorized by this issue.

title: 非破坏性 revise_intent 自锁：sidecar 写入未 stage，被自身 drift 检查拒绝
body:
## 复现（插件 3.6.5）

对任一 enrolled 任务（sidecar 路径在 scope_hint 内、worktree 干净）调用 `imm_kernel_canary` 的 `revise_intent`，next_intent 含任何内容变更（例如 verification descriptor 的 `timeout_ms` 调整）：

```
mutation_failed: task scope contains unstaged or untracked changes: docs/plans/<task>/...intent.json
```

## 根因

`executeOrdinaryOperation`（.pi-extension/imm-canary-work.ts）在 `app.execute` 之前把 next_intent 写入 sidecar 但**不 git add**。随后 kernel 的 `taskRevisionSnapshotOnce` drift 检查（unstaged scoped changes）把刚写入的 sidecar 判为脏文件，必然抛错；catch 再把字节还原。对任何内容变更型修订，该路径 100% 失败。

破坏性修订路径（`approve_breaking_intent_revision`，kernel_ports.ts 与同文件 authorize 流程）对同一写入执行 write + `git add`，drift 检查因此通过——证明 stage 是预期语义。

## 修复

c3d734f：revise_intent 与 breaking 路径对齐——写入后 `git add` sidecar（worktree == index，drift 检查放行，staged 相对 enrollment base 的变更是允许状态），失败时按 `ls-files --stage` 快照精确还原 index 与字节。

## 备注

- `revise_intent` 经 `applyTaskAction` 强制要求 compatible 分类（goal/owner/scope/assertion 不变），仅 descriptor 参数（如 timeout_ms）调整是唯一合法的非破坏性修订场景，正是被自锁挡死的场景。
- 插件模块被 Pi 运行时缓存，修复需完整重启 Pi 会话后生效。

## How to use this Issue

- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites or closes this Parent after creation; the tracker never changes or closes it automatically.

## Problem

A whole-system review found six defects, each reproducible at the released version. Packaged contracts instruct a Host to call tools that do not exist on it, including a freeze step the Kernel already performs internally. Two guardrails assert a source-text spelling rather than the behavior they stand for, so legitimate evolution reads as guardrail weakening. A batch authorization expires after ten minutes while the default batch budget is eight hours, and one Host re-opens the native gate on every resume. Spec binding is resolved only from the freeze path, so a scope_hint missing its bound Spec paths fails after an Executor has written the code — and only 8 of 32 recorded tasks complete single-pass. The two Host adapters share about two thirds of their batch gate lines and already carry four uncovered behavioral divergences. A closed 2,277-line retired surface and 30 unreachable validator exports still build, still ship, and are still maintained.

## Result

Packaged contracts are Host-neutral about tool identity and a guard prevents regression. Both guardrails assert behavior. One batch authorization spans the budget the user confirmed, and a resume reuses it instead of re-prompting. A missing Spec binding is refused at the enrollment gate and excluded at batch planning time, before implementation. Batch preflight and batch reason prose are decided once below the Host boundary, the four divergences converge on the safer branch, and terminal GitHub projection no longer depends on which Host settled the task. The retired surface is deleted and the package file list matches the remaining tree, while the TaskRecord v3 read path, the legacy audit reader, and the storage layout migration are explicitly retained. The three genuinely open unattended-Review questions are recorded as ADR drafts.

## Initiative design

Invariants: dependency direction stays adapter to shared runtime to Kernel, and the prohibited coupling removed here is adapter-to-adapter-by-copy. Shared runtime imports no Host SDK and branches on no Host identity; ADR-0004's rejection of a generic Host registry stands. A Batch Authorization remains one literal-user Enrollment act per ADR-0005 Decision 1, and enrollment remains the single native gate — no slice adds a second human stop. Ordering: S1, S2, S3, S4, S7, S13 and S14 are independent and may proceed in parallel; S5 and S6 follow S2 so that a deletion never has to edit a guard it would otherwise trip; S8 follows S7 because it reuses the module S7 extracts; S9 follows S2, S3 and S4 because it moves the code they change; S10, S11 and S12 follow S9 because they build on the shared preflight. Shared interfaces and state flow: a new Kernel module resolves Spec binding for enrollment, freeze, and batch planning from one implementation; a new shared preflight module projects claim, branch, cleanliness, recovery children, plan digest and base HEAD for both adapters; a new frozen table is the sole producer of batch reason and recovery strings. Batch authorization moves from absent to authorized to resumed, expired or consumed, with expiry bound to the confirmed budget deadline and every fail-closed clock and issuance check unchanged. Compatibility: this Initiative contains no externally breaking contract change. No published tool signature changes, no stored record shape changes, and no settled audit record is rewritten. The one intended user-visible restriction is that a TaskIntent whose scope_hint omits its bound Spec paths stops enrolling and must be revised, which is detected at the gate rather than after work is lost. Four slices are critical and are therefore never eligible for an unattended batch.

## Decisions

- Packaged contracts name the obligation, not a Host's tool spelling; the stale freeze instruction is deleted because the Kernel already performs it and no Host gains a tool.
- Guardrails assert behavior: produced Git argument vectors for the worktree prohibition, and production imports for the retired validator exports.
- Authorization lifetime and gate-per-batch are two separate invariants, authorized, verified and rolled back separately.
- Spec binding becomes an enrollment precondition and a batch planning filter; freeze-time enforcement is retained, not replaced, because enrollment cannot observe post-implementation scope drift.
- Host-independent pure functions move to the layer that already owns batch state; each adapter keeps only its confirmation transport, failure envelope shape, and non-interactive refusal form.
- Existing divergences converge on the safer branch; actor identity is settled separately under critical risk and migrated only forward.
- The validator reduction is compiler-driven: symbols are de-exported first and typecheck decides what is truly unreachable. A name-list deletion is not permitted.
- Unattended Review disposition is recorded as three ADR drafts with options and recommendations; drafting records the decision space, it does not settle it.

## Testing strategy

Every slice verifies through focused suites that already exist, except one new packaged-contract guard that fails against the pre-change contracts, which is the evidence it catches the regression it names. The two deletion slices additionally verify through typecheck, because a closed island is proven closed by the compiler rather than by a passing test run. Two failure modes are guarded explicitly: a suite that passes because coverage was deleted, addressed by requiring every removed test to either protect a now-absent behavior or name the surviving test that still covers it; and a suite that passes tautologically, addressed by retiring the parity assertions that the shared reason table makes vacuous and restating their property as one that can still fail. Cross-Host behavior is pinned by the dual-host conformance suite, which gains a scenario for each converged divergence.

## Out of scope

- Removing the review-submission verdict echo, making the pre-flight status read advisory, and folding unknown-settlement reconciliation into an ordinary projection read: all three alter a published Host tool contract and need a compatibility window.
- Implementing anything the three ADR drafts decide.
- Multi-worktree batches, ref pushes, pull-request creation, and cron or CI-hosted runs: deferred by ADR-0005 and not reopened here.
- A generic Host registry or any Host-identity branch inside shared runtime: rejected by ADR-0004.
- Deleting the TaskRecord v3 read path, the legacy audit reader, or the storage layout migration.
- Rewriting actor identity inside already-settled audit records.
- Any change to deterministic QA execution or to the existence of the single enrollment native gate.

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=wc-host-neutral-contract-tool-names --> **wc-host-neutral-contract-tool-names**: No packaged contract instructs a Host to call a tool that does not exist there.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=wc-behavioral-guardrails --> **wc-behavioral-guardrails**: Two guardrails fail on the regression they name instead of on a spelling.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=wc-batch-resume-single-gate --> **wc-batch-resume-single-gate**: Resuming an authorized batch reuses its authorization instead of opening a second native gate.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=wc-batch-authorization-lifetime --> **wc-batch-authorization-lifetime**: One batch authorization spans the budget the user actually confirmed.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=wc-retire-authority-observation-island --> **wc-retire-authority-observation-island**: A closed 2,277-line retired surface stops shipping and stops being guarded. (blocked by: wc-behavioral-guardrails)

title: [wcr-remediation] Workflow consolidation remediation
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=workflow-consolidation-remediation -->

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites or closes this Parent after creation; the tracker never changes or closes it automatically.

## Problem

A two-axis code review of the workflow-consolidation Initiative (Slices S1-S14) found 13 concrete findings: a settled-batch resume path that can inherit a stale budget and deadline, duplicated authorization logic still living in two Host adapters instead of one shared module, a terminal-tracker projection that can misfire a rollback after a mutation already committed, tests that pass even when the behavior they claim to guard is absent, superseded test guards left in place alongside their replacements, missing-path detail dropped from a Spec-binding failure message, batch tests that assert against their own internal call instead of observed behavior, a retired test's coverage with no named successor, three ADRs left in a proposed state that read as settled decisions, orphaned imports from the S9/S13 refactor, duplicated literal strings in one Host adapter, an unnecessarily eager status projection on every advance, and a frozen TaskIntent verification descriptor that can no longer be re-verified once the host runner version moves forward.

## Result

Each of the 13 findings is fixed or explicitly accepted as a tradeoff, Slice by Slice, with focused acceptance criteria tracing back to the original evidence: the resume path uses a single correct signal instead of two diverging ones, the duplicated Host logic converges into one shared module, the terminal-tracker projection can no longer replay a committed mutation, the weakened tests are rewritten to fail when the guarded behavior regresses, superseded guards are retired in favor of their replacements, the Spec-binding failure names the actual missing paths, the batch tests assert observed execution instead of an internal call, the retired coverage gets a named successor, the three ADRs reach a final status, the orphaned imports and duplicated strings are removed, the status projection runs only when needed, and the frozen-runner tradeoff is recorded in a dedicated decision record with no code change.

## Initiative design

One Parent Initiative Issue tracks 14 Child Slices, each bound to its own TaskIntent and Spec. Three critical-risk Slices (the resume-signal fix, the shared preflight extraction, and the terminal-tracker mutation-safety fix) go through native Enrollment with independent review before merge; seven material-risk Slices repair test validity, guard coverage, and duplicated logic; four routine Slices close out documentation, naming, and dead-code cleanup, including one ADR-only Slice with no code change. Execution proceeds in dependency order: the resume-signal fix first, the shared preflight extraction second, and the remaining Slices in parallel once their blockers clear.

## Decisions

- Route every fix through the Managed Path (Spec plus TaskIntent, then native Enrollment) rather than editing Kernel or Host-adapter code directly, since this repository's own authorization system is what is being repaired.
- Accept that Slices S1, S2, and S3, already settled before the host runner moved from 1.3.14 to 1.4.2, lose their frozen re-verification path; going forward, protection against their regressing rests on the standing test suite on main, not on re-opening a frozen artifact.
- Classify the import and string-cleanup Slices as material risk rather than routine, because their fixes rewrite existing test assertions rather than only deleting dead code.

## Testing strategy

Each Slice's acceptance criteria trace to the specific file and line evidence that produced the finding; critical- and material-risk Slices add or rewrite a failing-first test that reproduces the original defect before the fix, then close on bun test and bun run typecheck passing; the routine ADR-only Slice has no test, only a documentation acceptance.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the Kernel or Host-adapter authority model beyond the 13 findings from the S1-S14 review.
- Re-opening or re-verifying the already-settled S1, S2, and S3 TaskIntents.

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM1 --> **RM1**: Fix batch_preflight.ts so a settled (non-active) batch record never causes a fresh batch to inherit a stale budget or be reconstructed as already-settled: is_resuming must be computed once from activeRecord !== null and used identically for both the budget-inheritance decision and the reported projection field.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM2 --> **RM2**: Finish the S9 preflight extraction that CONTEXT.md:215 says runtime/unattended/ already owns exclusively: move the reuse/expiry decision, the BatchAuthorizationBinding construction, and the post-gate claim/drift cascade out of runtime/claude/kernel_ports.ts and .pi-extension/imm-unattended-batch.ts into runtime/unattended/, so both adapters become callers only. (blocked by: wcr-batch-resume-budget-drift)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM3 --> **RM3**: Stop kernel_ports.ts's terminal-tracker projection from running inside the authorize try/catch that owns Kernel-mutation rollback: a projection failure after the underlying Kernel mutation has already committed must never trigger restoreStagedIntent() or rethrow in a way a caller could read as 'the mutation did not happen' and retry.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM4 --> **RM4**: Fix tests/packaged-contract-tool-surface.test.ts so a contract token present on zero Host tool surfaces is reported as a failure (the exact HTN-2 regression it exists to catch), and its pre-change comparison reads the actual pre-S1 file content instead of a hardcoded paraphrase.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM5 --> **RM5**: Complete S2's guardrail migration: remove the regex/spelling-based assertions in tests/unattended-contracts.test.ts and tests/v3-island-deletion.test.ts that the new behavioral guards were meant to replace, once the behavioral guards' coverage is extended to plugins/immune-brain/.pi-extension/ and plugins/immune-brain/runtime/claude/ (the two guard sets currently check neither directory).
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM6 --> **RM6**: Make inspectSpecBinding's unpaired-path binding_missing fallback (runtime/kernel/spec_binding.ts, reached when non-empty active/archived scope_hint paths exist but never pair into exactly one binding) name the concrete unpaired paths instead of returning an empty missing array and a generic message, and make batch_plan.ts render that detail; remove the unreachable SPEC_BINDING_REASONS.binding_incomplete dead-code entry.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM7 --> **RM7**: Replace two weak assertions with execution-driven ones: tests/unattended-batch-plan.test.ts's binding-refusal case currently compares batch_plan's output to the same inspectSpecBinding call batch_plan makes internally instead of driving enrollCanary's refusal path, and two dual-host-assurance-conformance.test.ts scenarios prove adapter routing via source-text includes() on the adapter files instead of executed behavior.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM8 --> **RM8**: Record the successor for the ISL-2 coverage removed with tests/kernel-r2a-boundary.test.ts (an unrecognized runKernelCommand invocation refuses with invalid_command and writes nothing to authoritative state): tests/kernel-shadow-cli.test.ts already asserts this generically for an unknown command; extend it to also cover the literal 'readiness' token so the original scenario is preserved, not just an arbitrary placeholder string, and name it as ISL-2's successor.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM9 --> **RM9**: Update docs/adr/0008-batch-capability-rehydration.md so its description of where the batch-authorization reuse decision lives matches the shared runtime/unattended/ implementation completed by wcr-complete-shared-batch-preflight, instead of the pre-remediation claim. (blocked by: wcr-complete-shared-batch-preflight)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM10 --> **RM10**: Resolve docs/adr/0006-unattended-review-dispatch-authority.md and docs/adr/0007-parked-child-claim-release.md out of their 'proposed'/'Decision: Not settled' state: since the code implementing each decision already shipped in S1-S14, finalize each ADR's status to reflect the decision actually taken, matching CONTEXT.md's definition of an ADR as a settled, hard-to-reverse decision.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM11 --> **RM11**: Remove the unused imports S9/S13 left behind in kernel_ports.ts, imm-unattended-batch.ts, and imm-canary-work.ts, and enable noUnusedLocals in tsconfig.json so bun run typecheck catches recurrence instead of relying on review. (blocked by: wcr-complete-shared-batch-preflight)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM12 --> **RM12**: Extract the TUI-refusal/recovery strings repeated verbatim within .pi-extension/imm-unattended-batch.ts into one local helper, and move or correct the stale isOwnBatchClaim comment that now describes code living in batch_preflight.ts.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM13 --> **RM13**: Stop kernel_ports.ts's withTerminalTracker from running a full this.status() call for every advance/submitReview/authorize invocation regardless of whether the call is terminal; only pay that cost when the underlying operation actually reached a terminal state.
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=RM14 --> **RM14**: Author docs/adr/0009-settled-slice-reverification-loss.md recording the accepted decision that settled TaskIntents (S1/S2/S3, frozen at runner_version 1.3.14) permanently lose their frozen re-verification path once the host runner moves past that version, and that re-verification protection for settled Slices going forward is main's standing test suite's responsibility, not a re-openable frozen artifact. No runtime or test code changes.

title: [工作流简化] 简化状态、契约、Scope 与验收工作流
body:
<!-- immune-brain-tracker:v1 -->
<!-- immune-brain:kind=initiative -->
<!-- immune-brain:repo-id=1337032642 -->
<!-- immune-brain:initiative-id=managed-workflow-simplification -->

## How to use this Issue

- Edit planning prose and Slice ordering directly after creation.
- Keep each Slice marker attached to exactly one stable Slice entry.
- The tracker never rewrites or closes this Parent after creation; the tracker never changes or closes it automatically.

## Problem

多文件状态协调、重复规划产物、逐文件范围预测与无效审查往返增加执行和恢复成本。

## Result

完成 SQLite 单一状态、最小执行契约、弹性范围与完整快照验收，并通过显式迁移退出旧机制。

## Initiative design

技术基线：docs/specs/managed-workflow-simplification.spec.md；每个 Child 使用独立绑定的 Spec。S1 建立 worktree-local SQLite 与精确 run 身份；S2 简化 Intent/Spec 与稳定路径；S3 确保范围内探索和完整快照验收；S4 缩短验收并区分建议和有据阻塞；S5 完成迁移、清理与打包。各项串行，作为一次 major upgrade 交付。Git 保存交付对象，数据库保存运行事实，终态审计为可重试导出。当前运行中的任务不迁移自身数据库。

## Decisions

- 每个 worktree 独立数据库；数据库和备份不进 Git，schema/迁移与审计可版本管理。
- 任务与执行分离；快照和审计按工作区/运行命名，避免相互覆盖。
- 简单任务无需重复 Spec；目录内发现新文件不补批，真实越界仍需授权。
- 冻结绑定不可变对象；完整 QA 和必要审查使用同一交付身份。
- 无长期双写；旧运行时在 S5 删除，只读 importer 在下一 major 退出。

## Testing strategy

各 Child 使用聚焦本地行为测试验证自身结果；跨宿主、迁移中断、多工作区与打包在集成验收中覆盖。最终运行发布就绪检查，但本 Initiative 的规划与实施本身不发布版本。

## Out of scope

- 仓库级任务去重、远程共享数据库、通用调度框架
- 自动创建或切换 worktree
- 规划期间的代码实现、实际数据迁移、提交推送、安装和发布

## Slices

- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S1 --> **S1**: 同一工作区使用单一事务状态；明确区分任务与执行，消除多文件 owner 不一致。
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S2 --> **S2**: 简单任务不再生成重复 Spec；复杂设计仍绑定验收，冻结与返工不搬文件。 (blocked by: mws-sqlite-authority)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S3 --> **S3**: 范围内发现新文件可继续；遗漏文件和用户改动污染在验收前暴露。 (blocked by: mws-minimal-intent)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S4 --> **S4**: 正常验收自动推进；建议不阻塞，有据缺陷保留返工和复审。 (blocked by: mws-delivery-scope)
- [ ] <!-- immune-brain:slice-id=S5 --> **S5**: 迁移与恢复可验证，旧写入机制退出，完整升级具备发布条件。 (blocked by: mws-assurance-review)

---

An Open Issue only means the Task still needs attention; only a claimless terminal projection closes it (`done` → Completed, `stopped` → Not planned)._
